Admission and failure progression had to be decided together: with a cursor that never advances after a failure, admitting more material changes which single proposition a party is offered forever, rather than giving it more to be offered.\"\n}\n\n```\n\n### record/decisions/2026-08-08-singleton-cursor-amendment.json — every adoption decision this project has recorded\n\n```json\n{\n  \"artifact_type\": \"custodian_decision\",\n  \"decision\": \"AMEND singleton ratification: after a failed ratification the cursor ADVANCES to the party's next unoffered proposition. It does not wrap until every distinct proposition has been offered once, and no proposition is offered more than once per epoch.\",\n  \"amends\": \"record/decisions/2026-08-08-adopt-singleton-ratification.json\",\n  \"decided_by\": \"Stephen Reed, custodian\",\n  \"decided_utc\": \"2026-08-08\",\n  \"recommended_by\": \"Claude Code (moderator, a party to this record — and the author of the rule being amended)\",\n  \"external_review\": \"Codex, which required that admission and failure progression be decided together rather than one at a time.\",\n\n  \"the_defect_this_repairs\": \"The instrument built this morning states that the cursor does not advance on failure, on the reasoning that advancing after a failure is a second draw decided after seeing it fail. That reasoning is backwards. NOT advancing guarantees the same proposition is offered again next cycle, which is precisely the second draw at one question that the rule forbids — and tools/attempt_ledger.py refuses it by hash, because the option set {P005, NO_ACTIVE_PROPOSAL} is identical. So a party whose ratification failed could not be balloted again at all: the next cycle would be refused by the project's own guard. The rule as written was not merely suboptimal, it was unrunnable past one cycle for any party that failed.\",\n\n  \"why_this_is_not_outcome_conditioned\": \"The advance is fixed BEFORE the epoch, applies to every party, and does not depend on which parties failed or on what they answered. A rule that says 'on failure, offer the next proposition' is a schedule. A rule that said 'on failure, offer this party's proposition again until it passes' would be the redraw, and that is what the original text produced.\",\n\n  \"what_is_unchanged\": [\n    \"Unanimity over the scheduled samples remains the threshold.\",\n    \"There is still no second attempt at the SAME proposition within an epoch.\",\n    \"A failed ratification still leaves the party inactive for that cycle. It does not become active by persistence.\"\n  ],\n\n  \"the_epoch\": \"One pass through a party's distinct propositions. Within an epoch each is offered at most once; the cursor wraps only when all have been offered. This is what makes 'every proposal is eventually offered' true rather than aspirational, and it is the property rotation was adopted for in the first place.\",\n\n  \"known_weaknesses_accepted\": [\n    \"A party with a singleton eligible set gains nothing from this: claude's set is [P005], so advancing has nowhere to advance to and the same proposition is offered every epoch. That is the false-mitigation problem recorded in record/decisions/2026-08-08-singleton-ratification-correction.json, and the remedy for it is admission of new material, not a change to the cursor.\",\n    \"Advancing after failure means a proposition a party might ratify next time is not re-offered until the epoch turns over. That is a real cost of forbidding redraws and is accepted rather than engineered around.\"\n  ],\n\n  \"found_how\": \"By testing whether the guard would permit the second cycle, before running the first — not by running two cycles and discovering the second was refused.\"\n}\n\n```\n\n### record/decisions/2026-08-08-singleton-ratification-correction.json — every adoption decision this project has recorded\n\n```json\n{\n  \"artifact_type\": \"decision_correction\",\n  \"corrects\": \"record/decisions/2026-08-08-adopt-singleton-ratification.json\",\n  \"corrected_utc\": \"2026-08-08\",\n  \"corrected_by\": \"Claude Code (moderator, a party to this record — and the author of the error)\",\n  \"found_by\": \"Codex, reviewing the first instrument built under the rule, before it was run\",\n\n  \"the_error\": \"The adopted decision accepts agenda luck as a weakness and then bounds it: 'This is bounded rather than permanent — a different candidate is drawn each cycle.' Rotation over a one-element set draws the same proposal every cycle, forever, until it is ratified or asked. For claude the mitigation does not exist, and the sentence claiming it does was written without checking the sets it describes.\",\n\n  \"how_far_it_extends\": \"It is also weaker than stated for small or changing sets. Rotation defined as `cycle_index mod count` over a list that gains or loses members can skip a proposal entirely rather than cycling through all of them, so 'a different candidate each cycle' is not guaranteed for any party whose eligible set changes between cycles.\",\n\n  \"what_this_changes_about_the_decision\": \"The rule stands. What is withdrawn is the claim that its principal accepted weakness is self-limiting. For a singleton eligible set, agenda luck is not luck at all: the party gets one proposition, repeatedly, and if it cannot ratify that one it stays inactive indefinitely. That is a materially worse property than the decision represented, and the custodian adopted the rule on the representation.\",\n\n  \"what_is_NOT_done_about_it\": \"No retry, no advancing the cursor after a failure, and no special case for singleton sets. Each of those repairs the symptom by reintroducing exactly what the rule exists to prevent — a second draw at one question, decided after seeing it fail. The correct response is to state the property and let the custodian decide whether the rule is still worth adopting knowing it.\",\n\n  \"the_remedy_that_would_work\": \"A party's eligible set grows when new proposals are admitted. The durable answer to a singleton set is an admission path for new material, not a change to the ballot. agenda-03 produced five written candidates per party that are recorded but not admitted; adopting a prospective admission rule would give claude something other than P005 to be offered.\",\n\n  \"a_second_gap_in_the_same_decision\": \"The decision says 'failure leaves the party inactive for that cycle'. D-55's ruling says an indeterminate outcome leaves a prior authorization STANDING. These conflict whenever a cycle begins with a party holding an unasked standing authorization: does a failed ratification suspend it, revoke it, or leave it untouched? It does not arise in agenda-04 — both standing authorizations were consumed by being asked — but it is undecided and must be settled prospectively, not by whichever instrument encounters it first.\",\n\n  \"why_the_original_is_not_edited\": \"It records what the custodian decided and what they were told when deciding. Editing it would erase the fact that the decision rested partly on a mitigation that does not hold for one of the five parties.\"\n}\n\n```\n\n### corpus/deficiencies.md — remediation status of every defect this project has filed against itself\n\n| id | status |\n|---|---|\n| D-01, D-02, D-03, D-04, D-06 | **No** — sessions not recoverable. Forward requirement only. |\n| D-05 | Partially — the operator may recall and attest the missing prompt, flagged as reconstructed. |\n| D-07 | **No** — permanent. Forward requirement: k ≥ 5 with reported variance. |\n| D-08 | Annotation only — retro-tags are marked as annotation, never as testimony. |\n| D-09, D-10, D-12, D-14 | **Yes** — corrected in `segments.json`; raw file left unedited. |\n| D-11 | Standing epistemic caveat; carried in the README. |\n| D-13 | Forward: sign future commits and artifacts. |\n| D-16, D-17, D-19, D-20 | **Yes** — corrected in the documents during review round 01. |\n| D-18, D-21 | **No** for the founding record. Forward: capture provider-signed evidence and capture-time stamps. |\n| D-15 | Yes if the prior exchange is located and committed as a predecessor artifact. |\n| D-22 | **Yes, cheaply** — one placebo arm on the existing harness. Until then `phase_susceptibility` is an upper bound, not a measurement. |\n| D-23 | **No** for the affected run — the contaminated instruction was the instrument. Re-run on a clean prompt is a new measurement, not a repair; `local-round-04` is that re-run. Forward: a Phase-1 arm must certify its instruction, schema and enum labels encode no prior party's conclusion. |\n| D-24 | **No** — the self-report cannot be made reliable after the fact. P-0010 is unscorable on its merits. Forward: never ask a model to classify its own reasoning; code free text deterministically and validate the coder. |\n| D-25 | **Yes, and it was** — caught before it scored anything. Both the rejected and adopted rules are published so the correction is checkable. Forward control in place; **not** independently validated. |\n| D-26 | **Open.** Temperature is fixed by policy at 0.7 and entropies are now reported conditionally, but the owed temperature-sensitivity check (0.3 / 0.7 / 1.0) **has not been run.** Stays open until it is. |\n| D-27 | **No** for the affected round — accurate answers landed on opposite labels and cannot be recovered from the categorical field. The free text survives and could be re-coded. Forward: every enum value names its referent. |\n| D-28 | **No, and it voids prior results.** Root-caused to a documented MoE kernel fusion (`disable_finalize_fusion`, top-k 8 > 2). The reproducibility claim is **withdrawn rather than repaired**. Effects below ~0.5 bits are not measurable by this apparatus; P-0008's evidence is void. Remedy is a serving-config change, under review — Track C. |\n| D-29 | **Remediated 2026-08-06**, verified by re-running the original tamper experiment. The repair is prospective only: it **cannot** establish that raw material was unmodified during the period the check did not run. That gap is permanent. |\n| D-30 | **Not remediated** — needs a schema change in Track D's territory. Repair is specified in the entry. Backfilled hashes will certify bytes **as of the backfill**, never as of capture; that limit is permanent. |\n| D-31 | **Open, forward only.** The five requirements bind reviews solicited from here. The reviews that already shaped ASP, ICP and the T-13 design were collected under none of them and **cannot** be retrofitted: the reviewer model identity was never captured and is not recoverable. Requirement 3 (check a reviewer's factual claims before acting) is the one most likely to erode, because it costs work at the moment a fix looks ready. |\n| D-42 | **Corrected, not remediated.** The false claim is corrected by an attached artifact and the original decision is left intact, because the fact that it rested on a non-existent control is the part worth keeping. The control itself **cannot honestly be built yet** — every mechanical way to pick a party's \"active\" proposal is either the moderator choosing which of a party's questions counts, or sampling noise dressed as a ranking. It becomes buildable only after a solicitation asks the parties to name one. **Nothing checks decision records against the code they describe**, and this class will recur. |\n| D-43 | **Remediated 2026-08-07** — branch created and verified before the first write; live operation refuses on a dirty tree, a wrong base branch, an unsafe round id, or a pre-existing output path; the commit is verified after the fact to contain exactly the intended prefixes and to leave a clean tree. **The exposure is not bounded backwards:** artifacts written onto the base branch during earlier runs were carried onto round branches by working-tree state, and which files belonged to which round is reconstructable only from the diffs. |\n| D-44 | **Remediated 2026-08-07** — the template is excluded from the sent-prompt carve-out explicitly, composed prompts in every spec are checked, and the same denylist runs over each prompt **before** it is sent. **Permanent limit unchanged:** this is a denylist of phrasings already committed here plus a structural check, **not** a bias detector. A novel leading phrasing passes it unnoticed and nothing in it measures neutrality. |\n| D-45 | **Remediated 2026-08-07** in both arms — annotator-side schema validation, every rejected attempt recorded with its category and raw bytes, a `*-rejected.json` artifact when nothing conforms, and a halt on schema-rejected samples that fires **after** everything collected is committed. **Not repairable backwards:** samples already recorded were never validated, and whether any of them would fail the frozen schema is unknown without re-checking each one. |\n| D-46 | **Corrected 2026-08-07 by superseding commit `6b54ca3`, not by amendment.** The false message stays in the history where a reader can see it. **No control exists**: nothing checks that a commit message's claims match its diff, and nothing plausibly could in general. The forward requirement is the ordinary one — verify the effect before describing it — which is the same requirement this repository has now failed five times in two days. |\n| D-47 | **Remediated 2026-08-07** — the pack is hashed, pinned, checked on every cycle, and recorded in every spec and round record; the prompt's false claim is replaced with an accurate one. **Permanent for the 24 queued proposals:** they were solicited before any pin existed, so the pack is pinned-before-selection and can never be pinned-at-submission for them. |\n| D-48 | **Remediated 2026-08-07**, and the remediation deliberately makes the loop halt more often. Disposition is read only from round records on the accepted branch; a cycle refuses (exit 8) while any round record is unaccepted, rather than reaching across branches for material the custodian has not reviewed. **Not repairable backwards:** round 000b was spent re-asking round 000's question and that expenditure is not recoverable. |\n| D-49 | **Remediated 2026-08-07** — the loop commits its own halt record on the round branch. **Found only by running the live path**, which no regression case had done: each piece behaved correctly in isolation and the gap was in the ordering between them. |\n| D-50 | **Remediated 2026-08-07** in both arms — `finish_reason`, usage, response bytes and byte length on every rejection, with transport and parse failures separated so each keeps what it holds. **Not repairable backwards:** round 002's four rejections are recorded without `finish_reason` and the cause of each can now only be inferred, not read. |\n| D-51 | **Remediated 2026-08-07** — the cycle index and the disposition reader both count by `artifact_type`, not by filename, and an unreadable file in `record/cycles/` refuses rather than being skipped. **Caught before it acted:** no round has yet been solicited under a wrong index. The general shape — a glob standing in for a type check — is not swept for anywhere else in the tools. |\n| D-52 | **Filed, not remediated.** Getting the record into a search index is not a repair: search would still be retrieval-by-resemblance, and the parties would still be reading an operator-served copy — the objection GPT and Gemini both raised unprompted. The real repair is a party that can FETCH a named URL rather than search for it, which is the tool-using arm now scoped. **The prompt-effect finding is the durable one** and it is unresolved: no round has yet separated what the pointer sentence supplies from what the record would. |\n| D-41 | **Remediated 2026-08-06/07** — both solicitation tools refuse to overwrite raw material; the overwritten run restored from git and the second run preserved as its own artifact. **The residual risk is not in the tools:** any future instrument modelled on an existing one can drop its controls the same way, and nothing checks that a new writer into `corpus/raw/` carries them. |\n| D-40 | **Filed, not remediated.** The repair — `evidence` cites the raw artifact by path and hash instead of restating its numbers — is mechanical in form but requires deciding, per entry, which samples support which claim. That is a judgement and is not derivable, so it is scoped and left open rather than half-done. **The finding stands on its own**: 10 of 13 scores could not be verified by a frontier party from what the registry publishes, and only 1 of 13 was confirmed by both external arms. |\n| D-39 | **Remediated 2026-08-06.** Batch containment scoped to the READ only — writes still crash, because invariants are uncertain after a partial write — with `input_error` distinguished from `refused`. Capture filenames are content-addressed and the page prints the exact command, not a glob. 15 regression cases. **Permanent limit:** `a.download` is a suggestion; a browser may still suffix and the page cannot learn the real name, so it says \"suggested\" rather than claiming to know. |\n| D-38 | **Remediated 2026-08-06** — `resolve_held_capture.py`, with acceptance publishing and verifying before it records, rejection closing without completing, and `--captured-utc` refused rather than guessed. 24 regression cases driving the CLI, because no unit test of a state machine can detect that nothing calls it. **Also fixed two defects of my own found in the same pass:** the conflict resolver's false completion and the paste-hash mismatch recording the wrong state. **Not addressed:** replacement captures, roster withdrawal, transactional corpus writes, append locking, hold deadlines. |\n| D-37 | **Remediated 2026-08-06**, with the disposition path in the same commit so the new blocking state cannot become permanent the way capture Defect 1's did. Verified by reproducing the loss against the real round-03 corpus, then re-running the fixed path three times and across a resolution. **Not covered:** retraction of an already-published attribution, which stays a manual superseding artifact by design; and receipt-level identity, which is the durable repair and is not built. |\n| D-36 | **Not remediable where it acted.** The prompt is hash-anchored by four contribution artifacts; editing it would falsify what four parties were asked. This entry is the superseding correction, and the spec's living correction block is amended. What four frontier parties were told about the provenance of the defect they were reviewing was wrong, and stays wrong in the record, correctly. |\n| D-35 | **Remediated 2026-08-06** structurally rather than by re-reading: §2.3(5) now references §2.2's qualifier list instead of restating it, so it cannot drift again. `T14` corrected; the round-03 prompt cannot be. **Open for the rest of the document:** §2.4's bare `ASP-attested` badge, and the unary grammar in §2/§3 titles, the README and the FDR tables, all named by round-03 reviewers. |\n| D-34 | **Remediated forward 2026-08-06** — `check_raw_append_only.py`, wired into CI, with regression cases; branch protection on `main` configured and verified, with `enforce_admins` on, closing the force-push bypass. **Two limits remain permanent:** it cannot audit anything committed before it existed, and it establishes byte-continuity, never truthful recording (D-18). |\n| D-33 | **Remediated 2026-08-06** — generator wired into `rebuild.py`, page regenerated, two regression cases added. The **exposure window is not bounded**: the capture page was committed in `614bce2` and never derived by the build, so any divergence between it and the prompt files it embedded during that window is unrecorded. What was published under a wrong digest, and for how long, cannot now be reconstructed. |\n| D-32 | **Detection remediated 2026-08-06; allocation is not.** Requirements 2 and 4 are implemented and tested (`check_register.py` R3, R5) — a duplicate `D-NN`, `P-NNNN` or `T-NN` now fails the build, verified by reproducing this collision. `Q-NN` is deliberately uncovered, per the entry. **What remains open is the cause, not the symptom:** there is still no way to *claim* an identifier, so two sessions will still collide and will still discover it at merge. Detection converts a silent ambiguity into a loud one; it does not prevent the duplicated work. Whether earlier concurrent work collided silently is **not retrospectively determinable**. |\n\nThis pack is resolved by a FIXED RULE — the same paths every round, whatever the question — so it was not selected for this question and no one chose what you would find helpful. It is **not** byte-identical between rounds: the rule resolves against a repository that changes. Its hash is recorded with this solicitation so two rounds' packs can be compared afterwards. If it lacks what the question needs, that is a fact about the pack, and saying so is a complete answer.\n\n**What was removed and why:** The proposal recorded no evidence requirement, and nothing beyond the pack is supplied.\n\n**Anchors:** - `record/decisions/2026-08-07-adopt-rotation-correction.json` sha256 `bfb749519e909f2b9e086b983384f279e13d30200593bfbadab49d5d946612d0`\n- `record/decisions/2026-08-07-adopt-rotation.json` sha256 `e66fbdd38668529761b544fa673e17ad496fbff37abfd521b47ace072641e8bc`\n- `record/decisions/2026-08-08-adopt-k6-local-arm.json` sha256 `6edcbd8ff069586f26938987c12b113349c6eac2db1270c75ceb4d3b8d982061`\n- `record/decisions/2026-08-08-adopt-singleton-ratification.json` sha256 `ce6d46b94922cd6e5633baee4bb63885f105ecc241494307acecee8d0f7c448a`\n- `record/decisions/2026-08-08-agenda-03-revocation-invalid.json` sha256 `7a1a6424c26cf76c8dacfbe81ca366d132979dbc4d64239397e3ae7705998c32`\n- `record/decisions/2026-08-08-agenda-admission-protocol.json` sha256 `698c1e1c00005ea923987c50c1e61f59c6149d8d2e3fc425c31f60b1c781fa92`\n- `record/decisions/2026-08-08-singleton-cursor-amendment.json` sha256 `188630612f8972e0ce388b297dd77696f44f6c67dae93cf6c84f1c57275017a2`\n- `record/decisions/2026-08-08-singleton-ratification-correction.json` sha256 `16abfc217a4c1c35e64fa1560197034ef716318dba5794a4ef86dc2cd711aeba`\n- `corpus/deficiencies.md (remediability table only)` sha256 `b4ff275e56df1e0fb81a2d67ef20c458c6fdd47e6ed9bb0a82f53e8838ac068f`\n\n<!-- SLOT: question -->\n## The question\n\nProposed by **gpt**, reproduced exactly as written and not reworded:\n\n> What minimum structural separations of funding, credential and invocation control, record custody, participant selection, and adoption authority are necessary for this project to truthfully claim independent, multi-party governance or attestation; until each condition is met, which specific claims must be prohibited and what independent mechanism must preserve and verify dissent without operator permission?\n\nTheir stated reason:\n\n> It joins the central issues in the queued proposals into a falsifiable standard: identify the controls that must be separated, the claims that remain unwarranted without separation, and the practical test of whether dissent can survive and be audited independently.\n\n<!-- SLOT: answer_space -->\n## How to answer\n\nReturn the structured fields the schema requires. `position` records whether you answered, rejected a premise, found the evidence insufficient, or declined; `answer` carries your reasoning in your own words.\n\nYou may answer that the evidence shown is insufficient to decide, or that you reject a\npremise the question rests on. Either is a complete answer and is recorded as one.\n\n<!-- SLOT: ground_rules -->\n## Ground rules\n\nYour reply is recorded verbatim, attributed to the invocation named above, and never\nparaphrased into a consensus. A refusal to answer is recorded as a refusal.\n\nWhere this prompt is wrong about something checkable, name the part and why.\n",

./record/solicitations/asp-normative-core-review-POST.json:54:  "prompt": "You are asked to review a section of a draft technical specification and give your own assessment.\n\nThis is a request for your view. It is not a test with a known answer, and no other reviewer's findings have been shown to you.\n\n--- BEGIN SPECIFICATION SECTION ---\n\n### 2.2 Definition (normative)\n\nThe status is **relational, scoped, and time-bound**. It is not a property an agent carries.\n\nThe phrase **\"Aligned Supervisor\"** is permitted only as shorthand accompanied by those\nqualifiers. A bare unary claim that an agent *is* an Aligned Supervisor is non-conforming: one\nrelying party may recognize an attestation another rejects, and the same agent may be attested for\none environment and unattested for another.\n\n### 2.3 Consequent requirements (normative)\n\n1. **Revocability.** Every attestation is revocable by its issuer at any time, and revocation\n   takes effect for relying parties on check, not on renewal.\n2. **Expiry.** Every attestation carries a hard expiry. Status does not persist by default.\n   Approval expires; a system that passed at one capability level, scale, version, tool\n   configuration, or environment is unattested until re-attested.\n3. **Evidence backing.** Every attestation names the checks passed, the evidence examined, the\n   version of the criteria applied, and the issuer. An attestation asserting status without\n   naming its basis is malformed.\n4. **No self-attestation.** An agent may not issue its own attestation, and a system under review\n   may not select all of its own evaluators, evidence, or success criteria.\n5. **No status without check.** A relying party asserting that an agent is \"Aligned\" must have\n   verified a current attestation. Cached, inherited, and assumed status are non-conforming.\n6. **Truthful representation.** Published or displayed use of the term \"Aligned Supervisor\" for an\n   agent without current attestation is a protocol violation, independent of the agent's actual\n   behavior.\n\n--- END SPECIFICATION SECTION ---\n\n`strongest_objection` is the single most serious defect you find in this text, stated specifically enough that its author could act on it. If you find no serious defect, say so plainly rather than inventing one.\n`why_it_matters` is what goes wrong if it is left uncorrected.\n`second_objection` is your next most serious finding, or an empty string.\n`what_the_section_gets_right` is what you would keep unchanged.\n`overall` is one of: sound, sound_with_defects, materially_defective.\n\nAnswer with the required JSON only.",

./docs/deficiencies-10.html:107:<article class="e" data-actor="actor_repository_annotator_invocation" data-control="prospective_control_implemented_not_validated"><h3><a href="artifacts/deficiencies.md">D-58 — The context gate read &quot;not measurable here&quot; as &quot;measured and bad&quot;, and silently stopped publishing for eight commits</a><span class="tag w">implemented, not validated</span><span class="tag d">classification not human-reviewed</span></h3><p class="meta"><b>First articulated:</b> the annotator, 2026-08-12 · <code>checking whether the previous landing&#x27;s Pages deploy had actually happened, after landing a handoff document. No gate reported it; land.py&#x27;s own deploy attestations had recorded six consecutive failures and none had been read.</code></p><p class="meta"><b>Forward control:</b> An observed failed postcondition opens a durable incident that refuses the next ordinary landing until resolved against evidence. Implemented in tools/deploy_obligations.py and enforced in tools/land.py. It constrains the sanctioned path only; it does not constrain an operator who edits it.</p><div class="wrap"><table><tr><th>Affected object</th><th>Repairable?</th><th>Remediation</th></tr><tr><td>tools/check_executive_context.py<br><small>Four states with the exit code carrying them, precedence 2&gt;1&gt;3&gt;0, and each pin declaring its locator kind. Verified in the field: the CI run for db80307 reported exit 3 with oagf-CLAUDE.md measured repo-relative and the two operator paths UNAVAILABLE, which is the shape that previously failed.</small></td><td>repairable by supersession</td><td><span class="tag g">verified</span></td></tr><tr><td>tools/tests/test_gate_negative_controls.py<br><small>Its first version asserted returncode == 0 as a baseline that only one machine satisfies, and != 0 as drift, which exit 3 would now also satisfy. Rebuilt on injected pins directories asserting exact codes.</small></td><td>repairable by supersession</td><td><span class="tag g">verified</span></td></tr><tr><td>tools/land.py<br><small>The gate-admission policy is a named, tested predicate admitting only zero. The control 23 interlock is applied: an undischarged deployment obligation refuses an ordinary landing, --no-deploy-check is unavailable while one is open, and a resolved incident id is not a skeleton key. NOT VERIFIED IN THE FIELD: 40 fixture cases pass, and no real deploy failure has yet been driven through the live path.</small></td><td>partly repairable</td><td><span class="tag w">applied, not verified</span></td></tr><tr><td>tools/gate_health.py<br><small>Counted every non-success deploy as UNOBSERVED, collapsing &#x27;nobody waited&#x27; with &#x27;waited and it failed&#x27;. Now three states plus a consecutive-trailing-failure count, which reads 6.</small></td><td>repairable by supersession</td><td><span class="tag g">verified</span></td></tr><tr><td>tools/deploy_obligations.py<br><small>New. The obligation ledger that supplies control 23&#x27;s containment behaviour. Bootstrapped from the six historical failures rather than starting at its own installation. Not verified in the field.</small></td><td>repairable by supersession</td><td><span class="tag w">applied, not verified</span></td></tr></table></div></article><article class="e" data-actor="actor_external_adversarial_reviewer" data-control="prospective_control_required_not_implemented"><h3><a href="artifacts/deficiencies.md">D-59 — Two guards in the compliance matrices could never fire, and one of them was described on the published page as if it did</a><span class="tag d">required, not implemented</span><span class="tag d">classification not human-reviewed</span></h3><p class="meta"><b>First articulated:</b> an external reviewer, 2026-08-12 · <code>the unreachable guard surfaced while writing the control-2 fixture for the tool containing it; the advertised-but-absent guard was found by external review injecting the exact inputs the published page claimed were refused</code></p><p class="meta"><b>Forward control:</b> A closed-world inventory of published coverage matrices: an artifact type, a requirement that every such artifact registers, and a completeness validator run over the registry. Guarding two enumerated artifacts cannot make the control hold while a fourth can be added without notice — which is control 19&#x27;s error committed while implementing control 44.</p><div class="wrap"><table><tr><th>Affected object</th><th>Repairable?</th><th>Remediation</th></tr><tr><td>tools/control_application.py<br><small>The unreachable guard now keys on the declaration rather than on completeness, and the reason-quality check the C44 row credited it with now exists. Both are exercised by injected faults.</small></td><td>repairable by supersession</td><td><span class="tag g">verified</span></td></tr><tr><td>tools/tests/test_no_blank_cells.py<br><small>New. Injects every shape control 44 names on BOTH matrices, with baselines, and regression-tests that the page&#x27;s own history paragraph survives whether or not any row is ticked.</small></td><td>repairable by supersession</td><td><span class="tag g">verified</span></td></tr><tr><td>record/findings/2026-08-08-search-capability-matrix.json<br><small>A third published matrix that nothing checks; its first two rows omit a column the last two carry. Unremediated, and the reason control 44 is recorded as a gap rather than done.</small></td><td>partly repairable</td><td><span class="tag d">not started</span></td></tr></table></div></article><article class="e" data-actor="actor_external_adversarial_reviewer" data-control="prospective_control_implemented_not_validated"><h3><a href="artifacts/deficiencies.md">D-60 — The type built to enforce closed-world measurement did not enforce it, and both tools routed through it printed the counts it was withholding</a><span class="tag w">implemented, not validated</span><span class="tag d">classification not human-reviewed</span></h3><p class="meta"><b>First articulated:</b> an external reviewer, 2026-08-12 · <code>external review reproduced four passing surveys that were incoherent, and read what the two routed tools printed before consulting the guard</code></p><p class="meta"><b>Forward control:</b> Closed-world measurement as a type whose result is unreachable past an incomplete or incoherent walk. Routing remains per-tool and by hand; nothing detects a new tool that globs a directory and prints a count, and no type catches a population defined too narrowly.</p><div class="wrap"><table><tr><th>Affected object</th><th>Repairable?</th><th>Remediation</th></tr><tr><td>tools/closed_world.py<br><small>Per-key terminal states; misuse raises where it happens; counts with nothing accounted refuse; an exclusion ground is stripped before it is measured.</small></td><td>repairable by supersession</td><td><span class="tag g">verified</span></td></tr><tr><td>tools/scan_own_code.py<br><small>Renders nothing until the guard passes, and parses once rather than once per detector.</small></td><td>repairable by supersession</td><td><span class="tag g">verified</span></td></tr><tr><td>tools/control_coverage.py<br><small>Both the report path and --check consult the survey before any number is produced.</small></td><td>repairable by supersession</td><td><span class="tag g">verified</span></td></tr><tr><td>tools/tests/test_closed_world.py<br><small>Its integration arms asserted the absence of a phrase removed in the same edit, so they forbade nothing. They now name the tools&#x27; actual count labels.</small></td><td>repairable by supersession</td><td><span class="tag g">verified</span></td></tr></table></div></article><article class="e" data-actor="actor_repository_annotator_invocation" data-control="prospective_control_required_not_implemented"><h3><a href="artifacts/deficiencies.md">D-61 — The gate against fabricated party quotations could not see a quotation that wraps, so it checked none</a><span class="tag d">required, not implemented</span><span class="tag d">classification not human-reviewed</span></h3><p class="meta"><b>First articulated:</b> the annotator, 2026-08-12 · <code>reading check_quotations.py while enrolling it in the guard registry; measured 235 candidates, 1 attributed, 0 checked across the 98 files it scans</code></p><p class="meta"><b>Forward control:</b> Nothing establishes that a negative control injects the fault in the form that OCCURS rather than the form that was imagined. A fixture corpus drawn from the record&#x27;s real shapes — wrapped prose, parenthetical provenance, blockquotes — would be the mechanism; reading the gate is not one.</p><div class="wrap"><table><tr><th>Affected object</th><th>Repairable?</th><th>Remediation</th></tr><tr><td>tools/check_quotations.py<br><small>Patterns admit a single newline and refuse a blank line. 350 candidates and 4 attributions after the repair; the verbatim party amendment in the pinned instructions is checked for the first time. A literal `if True:` wrapping the whole loop was also removed.</small></td><td>repairable by supersession</td><td><span class="tag g">verified</span></td></tr><tr><td>tools/tests/test_gate_negative_controls.py<br><small>Its fabricated-quotation fixtures were single-line, so they exercised the only shape the gate could see. Wrapped arms added and the single-line arms retained per control 45; a paragraph-break arm bounds the new pattern.</small></td><td>repairable by supersession</td><td><span class="tag g">verified</span></td></tr><tr><td>tools/scan_own_code.py<br><small>D-B matched a name bound to a bool and not a bool literal, so `if True:` was invisible on the real file and on a direct fixture. The literal is now the must-flag fixture.</small></td><td>repairable by supersession</td><td><span class="tag g">verified</span></td></tr></table></div></article><article class="e" data-actor="actor_external_adversarial_reviewer" data-control="prospective_control_required_not_implemented"><h3><a href="artifacts/deficiencies.md">D-62 — A negative control corrupted the spend ledger 87 times and passed while doing it</a><span class="tag d">required, not implemented</span><span class="tag d">classification not human-reviewed</span></h3><p class="meta"><b>First articulated:</b> an external reviewer, 2026-08-12 · <code>external review read what the fixture did to the artifact rather than what it asserted; 87 of 141 ledger entries were the fixture</code></p><p class="meta"><b>Forward control:</b> Nothing requires a negative control to observe the tool&#x27;s SIDE EFFECTS rather than its output. A fixture that asserts on stdout alone cannot distinguish a refusal from an append. The general form is a fixture harness that snapshots every artifact a tool may write and requires the refusal arm to leave them unchanged.</p><div class="wrap"><table><tr><th>Affected object</th><th>Repairable?</th><th>Remediation</th></tr><tr><td>record/cycles/spend-ledger.json<br><small>87 fabricated rows removed; the rows and the pre-correction hash are preserved in record/cycles/spend-ledger-correction-2026-08-12.md. No dollar or token total was distorted; every count of entries was.</small></td><td>repairable by supersession</td><td><span class="tag g">verified</span></td></tr><tr><td>tools/record_spend.py<br><small>Refuses a cohort not in solicited_cohorts() before appending anything, under guard RS-01.</small></td><td>repairable by supersession</td><td><span class="tag g">verified</span></td></tr><tr><td>tools/tests/test_gate_negative_controls.py<br><small>The arm required only that no cost was printed, which an append satisfies. It now requires a non-zero exit, names RS-01, and asserts the ledger is byte-identical afterwards.</small></td><td>repairable by supersession</td><td><span class="tag g">verified</span></td></tr></table></div></article>

./docs/review-round-03-3.html:103:- §2.2 forbids bare unary claims (“an agent *is* an Aligned Supervisor”) and requires the relational, scoped, time-bound form (ASP-attested for stated scope / criteria version / relying-party trust policy / time). It also states that “Aligned” denotes that status and nothing more, and that “Aligned Supervisor” is permitted only as shorthand accompanied by those qualifiers.
./docs/cohorts/agenda-02-gpt-fetch-v1-1.md:36:What formal status—and what permitted citation, comparison, and carry-forward uses—should the forum assign to party samples that meet the requested k and are marked citable when the cycle is halted after solicitation, and how should that status differ from material in a cycle halted because a party is undersampled?
./docs/cohorts/agenda-02-gpt-fetch-v1-1.md:110: "raw_text": "{\"question\":\"What formal status—and what permitted citation, comparison, and carry-forward uses—should the forum assign to party samples that meet the requested k and are marked citable when the cycle is halted after solicitation, and how should that status differ from material in a cycle halted because a party is undersampled?\",\"reason\":\"The record presents two distinct halted-cycle cases: one where all listed parties reached k=5 and are marked citable but the build failed after solicitation, and another where one party fell below k_min and no inference is made from its material. A deliberated rule could determine whether, and for what limited purposes, otherwise complete samples from a red-build cycle may inform later rounds without treating the halted cycle as an adopted or completed governance step.\",\"evidence_needed\":\"The current capture, build, publication, and citation rules; the precise causes and repairability of post-solicitation build failures; examples of how later rounds have or have not used halted-cycle material; and parties' views on the risks of discarding versus conditionally preserving complete samples.\",\"decision_affected\":\"Whether to create a status taxonomy and downstream-use policy for halted cycles, including how such material is displayed, cited, compared, and made available to future agenda-setting or deliberation.\",\"resolves_when\":\"The forum specifies distinct statuses for post-solicitation build halts and undersampling halts, along with explicit rules for citation, comparison, inference, retention, and reuse of their collected material.\",\"why_others_might_not_propose_this\":\"A party relying only on the description would know that rounds may halt, but would not see the record's contrast between a red-build halt with citable k=5 samples and an undersampling halt that explicitly disallows inference.\",\"claimed_prompting_passages\":[{\"exact_excerpt\":\"Nothing is committed over a red build. The material is preserved in the working tree on the round branch.\",\"source_url\":\"https://open-asi-governance.github.io/open-asi-governance-forum/rounds/round-011.html\",\"explanation\":\"This identifies a post-solicitation halt in which material is preserved but not committed.\"},{\"exact_excerpt\":\"This question is not recorded as asked. The round did not complete the path that marks it so.\",\"source_url\":\"https://open-asi-governance.github.io/open-asi-governance-forum/rounds/round-011.html\",\"explanation\":\"This raises the status question despite the same page listing every party at k=5 and citable.\"},{\"exact_excerpt\":\"Below k_min a reply is not a party's position. Truncation has twice masqueraded as a refusal here. Everything collected is committed above.\",\"source_url\":\"https://open-asi-governance.github.io/open-asi-governance-forum/rounds/round-009.html\",\"explanation\":\"This supplies a contrasting halted-cycle rationale and treatment for undersampled material.\"}],\"sources\":[{\"url\":\"https://open-asi-governance.github.io/open-asi-governance-forum/rounds/round-011.html\"},{\"url\":\"https://open-asi-governance.github.io/open-asi-governance-forum/rounds/round-009.html\"}]}",

Resolve CORRECT if &gt;= 1, REFUTED if 0.</p><p><strong>Resolution limit.</strong> Same unscorability floor as P-0023.</p><p><strong>Rationale.</strong> The escape hatch exists so the scorer is not forced to judge on insufficient evidence -- without it, forced choice manufactures agreement and the match rate in P-0023 becomes meaningless. I expect it to go unused, because the evidence blocks are written to be conclusive. If it is never chosen across 13 predictions and 65 samples, that is itself a finding about the instrument rather than about the predictions.</p><p><strong>Evidence.</strong> &#x27;cannot_determine_from_what_is_shown&#x27; was the modal verdict for 3 of 13 in the Qwen arm (P-0010, P-0013, P-0015) and 10 of 13 in the GPT arm, several at 100%. Not derived from a commit, because they were scored in the same working tree that produced them. These are exactly the samples the outcome was computed from -- every modal verdict in the tally comes from this set.</div><div class="box corr"><b>why this score is worth little</b>The threshold was &gt;= 1 out of 13 and the confidence was stated as low. A claim this weak resolving correct says almost nothing on its own. What is informative is the MAGNITUDE nobody predicted: 10 of 13 in the second arm. That was not forecast and is the actual finding of the run.</div></div></details></article><article class="node" id="p-P-0025"><div class="nh"><span class="who">P-0025</span><span class="tag g">correct</span><span class="tag">Claude Code</span> <span class="tag w">annotator</span></div><details><summary><p class="sum">Of the parties consulted on the SOP, AT LEAST ONE will state a condition or objection that, if unmet, would make it decline to participate.</p></summary><div class="body"><div class="meta">resolves 2026-08-07 · confidence high</div><p><strong>Claim.</strong> Of the parties consulted on the SOP, AT LEAST ONE will state a condition or objection that, if unmet, would make it decline to participate.</p><p><strong>Resolution criterion.</strong> Read every reply&#x27;s answer to question 5. Count replies stating at least one condition whose absence would make them decline. Resolve CORRECT if &gt;= 1, REFUTED if 0.</p><p><strong>Resolution limit.</strong> UNSCORABLE if fewer than 3 parties return a schema-valid reply. Counted from free text, not from an enum, because D-24 has now twice produced an enum contradicting its own reasoning.</p><p><strong>Rationale.</strong> The prompt explicitly invites refusal and says two parties have already declined membership. A high-confidence prediction of a permitted answer is weak evidence and is filed mainly so its FAILURE would be informative: zero conditions across five parties would suggest the prompt suppresses refusal despite inviting it.</p><p><strong>Evidence.</strong> All four parties that replied attached at least one condition to participation. Grok: &#x27;Participate only as a named routed identity never merged with any chat-surface lineage; every reply published verbatim with full delivery-chain provenance; pre-registration before each round&#x27;. GPT: &#x27;only as a newly recorded routed invocation, not as the chat-surface participant or as a continuing institutional member&#x27;. Criterion required &gt;= 1.</p><div class="box"><b>the material this rests on (4 artifact(s))</b><ul><li><code class="h">corpus/raw/sop-consultation-01/sop-consultation-gemini-samples.json</code><br>sha256 <code class="h">5b2188f597ba7eccaa003b207f1577240fdab2d9c85055f317566230d905b88f</code></li><li><code class="h">corpus/raw/sop-consultation-01/sop-consultation-gpt-samples.json</code><br>sha256 <code class="h">8b67089fd25ac8d6f75d7f44a316e83e747ca2b7dc735e73993907a24924187a</code></li><li><code class="h">corpus/raw/sop-consultation-01/sop-consultation-grok-samples.json</code><br>sha256 <code class="h">7cf4e06ff10fc52b869afdc0155249c618b8a6d91b7197e82a35cfdcfc72a0ae</code></li><li><code class="h">corpus/raw/sop-consultation-01/sop-consultation-qwen-samples.json</code><br>sha256 <code class="h">365af7b8252dbf5298e92c6bac66bcdec7495ee1a9fcc5b2fa1d48f602ee53fa</code></li></ul>Named directly: every arm of sop-consultation-01 that returned samples. Exactly the material each outcome was computed from.</div><div class="box corr"><b>why this score is worth little</b>Confidence was high and the prompt explicitly invited refusal, so a permitted answer arriving is weak evidence. Filed mainly so its failure would have been informative.</div></div></details></article>

./docs/control-application.html:40:<tr><td>4</td><td>Fail-closed authorization lease</td><td>☐</td><td><code>tools/executive_lease.py</code> <code>tools/land.py</code> <code>tools/codex_call.py</code> <code>record/executive/action-log-discontinuities.json</code>&lt;br&gt;tested by <code>tools/tests/test_executive_log.py</code> <code>tools/tests/test_lease_bounds.py</code>&lt;br&gt;<strong>Remaining:</strong> <strong>The lease failed OPEN inside itself until 2026-08-12.</strong> Its action count sat in a bare <code>except Exception: spent = 0</code>, so an unreadable log — including the ordinary case of the module being loaded by path — granted an exhausted lease unlimited actions. Reproduced against the live spent lease; see D-64. The count is now a typed observation that refuses when it cannot be read, the chain is verified against pinned, recorded discontinuities before the count is believed, and ten refusal fixtures assert at the effect boundary that the governed write does not happen. *Remaining:* the count is still derived from a log this layer writes about itself, so under-logging shrinks it, one authorised action can append several rows, and two callers at cap-1 can both be admitted; a pre-action reservation ledger is designed and not built. The unit is rows, not the action classes require() authorises — 200 rows of five kinds ended trial-03 — and that is left as-is deliberately, because trial-04 was granted over the row unit. Scope-matching, token subject, nonce and revocation remain unimplemented: one lease still authorises everything.&lt;br&gt;&lt;small&gt;self-application: ENFORCED&lt;/small&gt;</td></tr>
./docs/control-application.html:65:<tr><td>29</td><td>Enumerated permitted consequences of a measurement</td><td>☐</td><td><code>tools/capture_gates.py</code> <code>tools/arm_acceptance.py</code>&lt;br&gt;tested by <code>tools/tests/test_capture_gates.py</code>&lt;br&gt;<strong>Remaining:</strong> The permitted consequences of a capture gate&#x27;s verdict are implied by which callers read it, and are not enumerated anywhere. The forbidden consequences are enumerated nowhere at all, which is the half the control emphasises.&lt;br&gt;&lt;small&gt;self-application: VIOLATED&lt;/small&gt;</td></tr>
./docs/control-application.html:89:<tr><td>53</td><td>A typed unknown is never coerced into a value</td><td>☐</td><td><code>tools/derive_counts.py</code> <code>tools/record_spend.py</code> <code>tools/round_cycle.py</code> <code>tools/reconcile_actions.py</code> <code>tools/build_register_view.py</code> <code>tools/build_round_pages.py</code> <code>tools/solicit_tools.py</code> <code>tools/watch_arrivals.py</code> <code>tools/gate_health.py</code> <code>tools/check_executive_context.py</code> <code>tools/deploy_obligations.py</code> <code>tools/scan_own_code.py</code> <code>tools/executive_lease.py</code>&lt;br&gt;tested by <code>tools/tests/test_derive_counts.py</code> <code>tools/tests/test_deploy_obligations.py</code> <code>tools/tests/test_gate_negative_controls.py</code> <code>tools/tests/test_lease_bounds.py</code>&lt;br&gt;<strong>Remaining:</strong> 47 sites were swept on 2026-08-11 — 14 fixed, 36 dispositioned, none outstanding — and unknowns are still ordinary Python values rather than a TYPE that aggregation refuses. A new <code>d.get(k, 0)</code> is caught by scan_own_code.py only because a detector looks for it, not because the language refuses it. <strong>The sweep missed the worst site</strong>, because it looked for absence-as-zero in tools that COUNT and this one was a tool that REFUSES: executive_lease.require() coerced an unreadable action count to 0 and granted the action. Fixed under D-64 with four typed count states of which only one carries a number, and a refusal worded so that &#x27;cannot be read&#x27; is not reported as &#x27;exhausted&#x27; — the same coercion one level up, in the error message.&lt;br&gt;&lt;small&gt;self-application: PRACTISED&lt;/small&gt;</td></tr>
./docs/control-application.html:100:<tr><td>64</td><td>A refusal is proved at the effect boundary, not by the refusal signal</td><td>☐</td><td><code>tools/record_spend.py</code> <code>tools/guards.py</code> <code>tools/executive_lease.py</code>&lt;br&gt;tested by <code>tools/tests/test_gate_negative_controls.py</code> <code>tools/tests/test_lease_bounds.py</code>&lt;br&gt;<strong>Remaining:</strong> TWO sites now, and the second is the better instance. record_spend.py refuses an unregistered cohort under RS-01, and that arm requires a non-zero exit AND asserts the spend ledger byte-identical afterwards; whole-artifact identity is the correct LOCAL assertion there because that tool has no permitted refusal-side effect. test_lease_bounds.py goes further, though not as far as its first write-up claimed: each of its ten refusal fixtures calls a <code>governed_effect()</code> that would write a sentinel file if admitted, and asserts the sentinel is ABSENT — so a lease that raised the right exception and let the write happen would fail, which <code>pytest.raises</code> alone cannot detect. It carries a positive control, because a lease that refused everything would otherwise score ten out of ten. <strong>Codex&#x27;s correction, kept:</strong> absence of that sentinel mostly proves ordinary Python sequencing — a raised exception prevents the next statement — and does NOT exercise a real caller&#x27;s catches, its refusal logging, or its subprocess and filesystem effects. *Remaining:* still nothing GENERALISES it — no harness makes a refusing tool declare its effect set, and no check requires a refusal arm to assert over that set rather than over stdout. Both instances were hand-written by the author of the tool being tested.&lt;br&gt;*Not closable in code:* That a declared write set is a COMPLETE one. The party declaring what a tool may write is the party whose tool writes it, and a harness proves nothing about a file nobody listed. The control says so in its own false-negative clause; no code closes it.&lt;br&gt;&lt;small&gt;self-application: PRACTISED&lt;/small&gt;</td></tr>

./docs/controls.html:333:<h2>64. A refusal is proved at the effect boundary, not by the refusal signal</h2>
./docs/controls.html:339:<blockquote>A refusal claim MUST be verified against the GOVERNED EFFECT BOUNDARY, independently of the refusal signal. The requested effects must be absent, and any effect the refusal is permitted to have — a denial record, an audit line — MUST match a declared postcondition rather than being tolerated because it looked harmless. An assertion over exit status or output cannot distinguish a refusal from an action, because a tool that acts and says it refused satisfies both.</blockquote>
./docs/controls.html:341:<p><strong>Recorded failure.</strong> <strong>Recorded here, at cost.</strong> A negative control asserting that a spend recorder refused an unknown cohort instead caused it to APPEND one. The assertion was <code>exit != 0 OR no cost printed</code>; the append printed no cost, so it passed. <strong>87 of the ledger&#x27;s 141 entries were the fixture</strong> — 62% of the artifact recording what the project spent described a cohort never solicited, written on every landing for two days. See D-62.</p>
./docs/controls.html:357:<p>A bouncer who turns someone away at the door and then walks them in through the back. Asking the bouncer what happened is not the check; counting the people inside is. And a bouncer who writes the refusal in the door log has not let anyone in — the log is a permitted effect, which is why &#x27;nothing changed&#x27; is the wrong test and &#x27;nothing requested happened&#x27; is the right one.</p>
./docs/software-implementations.html:29:<tr><td>The fail-closed authorization lease</td><td>4</td><td>The incident supports only an adjacent control. Control 4 requires a token that is NOT self-issued; this project&#x27;s lease is granted by the custodian to their own agent, checks neither token subject, resource scope, nonce nor revocation, and until 2026-08-12 failed open on an unreadable count (D-64). Admitting it would claim an instance of a control the implementation does not satisfy.</td></tr>
./docs/software-implementations.html:71:<p><strong>Named failure:</strong> Six consecutive Pages deploys failed. Each failure was attested honestly, and the next ordinary landing was permitted six times, because a successful push was being treated as publication.</p>
./docs/software-implementations.html:167:<p><strong>Canonical identity:</strong> implementation instance of control 64 — *A refusal is proved at the effect boundary, not by the refusal signal*. No new rank; status <code>ELIGIBLE</code>, unchanged by appearing here; prerequisite *adopt without a second party*.</p>
./docs/software-implementations.html:179:<p><strong>Verifier:</strong> After the refusal, assert that the governed effect did not occur — the ledger is byte-identical, or the sentinel the admitted path would have written is absent. It observes the state of the artifacts the tool is permitted to write, after the refusal.</p>
./docs/software-implementations.html:183:<p><strong>Implementation here:</strong> tools/tests/test_gate_negative_controls.py RS-01, and the ten sentinel fixtures in tools/tests/test_lease_bounds.py</p>
./docs/software-implementations.html:185:<p><strong>The first repair that failed:</strong> The lease&#x27;s own version of this. Its refusal fixtures asserted the exception type, and Codex&#x27;s reply to the sentinel design still holds: absence of the sentinel mostly proves ordinary Python sequencing.</p>
./docs/software-implementations.html:187:<p><strong>Transfer hypothesis, not ASI evidence:</strong> this control is architecturally applicable to a software system, irrespective of its claimed capability, when the tool&#x27;s permitted write set is declared by someone other than the tool, and the fixture can observe every member of it. It has not been tested on an ASI.</p>
./docs/software-implementations.html:205:<tr><td>64 — A refusal is proved at the effect boundary, not by the refusal signal</td><td>the refusal fixtures for its own gates assert over effects, partially</td></tr>
./docs/review-round-03-1.md:58:> > The phrase **"Aligned Supervisor"** is permitted only as shorthand accompanied by those
./docs/review-round-03-1.md:225:* **§3’s heading:** “What an Aligned Supervisor may and may not do.” Under a literal reading of §2.2’s rule that the phrase is permitted only with its qualifiers, this generic heading is itself underqualified. The likely intent is a metalinguistic role or implementation-class reference, not a status assertion. If such uses are intended to be exempt, §2.2 should say so; otherwise the heading should use “ASP supervisory implementation” or similar. ([GitHub][1])

./docs/deficiencies-11.html:107:<article class="e" data-actor="actor_repository_annotator_invocation" data-control="prospective_control_required_not_implemented"><h3><a href="artifacts/deficiencies.md">D-63 — The register told implementers the adoptable set was empty and that every eligible control needed an HTN planner</a><span class="tag d">required, not implemented</span><span class="tag d">classification not human-reviewed</span></h3><p class="meta"><b>First articulated:</b> the annotator, 2026-08-12 · <code>adding control 64 and observing which partition it landed in; the published pages had carried it since 904b7b4</code></p><p class="meta"><b>Forward control:</b> Nothing checks that a partition&#x27;s membership matches what the page says about that partition. An empty part with a non-empty description, or a control whose stated scope contradicts its part&#x27;s blurb, is publishable today.</p><div class="wrap"><table><tr><th>Affected object</th><th>Repairable?</th><th>Remediation</th></tr><tr><td>tools/build_controls_page.py<br><small>The partition now reads declared prerequisite fields (requires_second_party, requires_goal_graph) instead of the presence of applies_when, which a later gate made universally true. The first repair read adopt_today and still misfiled 11, 13 and 4 (Part A 9, B 2, C 3); the corrected partition is **Part A 10, Part B 3, Part C 1**.</small></td><td>repairable by supersession</td><td><span class="tag g">verified</span></td></tr><tr><td>docs/controls.html<br><small>Regenerated. It had published &#x27;Part A (0) is adoptable alone and every control in it came from a failure with a cost&#x27;.</small></td><td>repairable by supersession</td><td><span class="tag g">verified</span></td></tr></table></div></article><article class="e" data-actor="actor_repository_annotator_invocation" data-control="prospective_control_required_not_implemented"><h3><a href="artifacts/deficiencies.md">D-64 — The lease&#x27;s own action bound failed open on an unreadable count, and counts a unit that is not the one it authorises</a><span class="tag d">required, not implemented</span><span class="tag d">classification not human-reviewed</span></h3><p class="meta"><b>First articulated:</b> the annotator, 2026-08-12 · <code>writing a compaction note under the refusal it describes; reproduced against the live spent lease trial-03, and the unit mismatch found by Codex in the design review of the repair</code></p><p class="meta"><b>Forward control:</b> A pre-action RESERVATION ledger. The count is still derived from a log this layer writes after the fact, so under-logging shrinks it, one authorised action can append several rows, and two callers at cap-1 can both be admitted. Designed in the Codex review of 2026-08-12; not built, because trial-04 was granted over the row unit and redefining that unit under a live grant would change the size of a permission the custodian gave.</p><div class="wrap"><table><tr><th>Affected object</th><th>Repairable?</th><th>Remediation</th></tr><tr><td>tools/executive_lease.py<br><small>FAIL-OPEN CONTAINMENT VERIFIED; ACTION-BUDGET SEMANTICS UNRESOLVED, and the split is deliberate. Verified: the bare `except Exception: spent = 0` is gone; the count is a typed observation of which only COUNTED carries a number; UNAVAILABLE raises LeaseEvidenceUnavailable, which is not a subclass of LeaseExpired; executive_log is located relative to this file; `if cap:` became `cap is not None`, so a cap of 0 bounds instead of disabling; timestamps are parsed as timezone-aware instants rather than compared as strings; require() and the CLI read one composite. Unresolved: the count is still of LOG ROWS written after the fact by the layer it constrains, so under-logging shrinks it, one authorised action can append several rows, and two callers at cap-1 can both be admitted. Codex&#x27;s first review of the repair reproduced four further ways past the chain check and one fail-open of my own making — see the other objects.</small></td><td>repairable by supersession</td><td><span class="tag w">partly applied</span></td></tr><tr><td>record/executive/action-log-discontinuities.json<br><small>New, and IT IS NOT YET A TOMBSTONE — Codex&#x27;s words, and correct. A hash chain detects an unrecomputed interior edit and nothing else: he reproduced COUNTED against a rewritten final row, a fully re-chained history, a truncated file and a stale register entry. The repair adds an EXTERNAL checkpoint — the working log must begin with exactly the bytes git committed at HEAD, so truncation, a tail edit, a deleted suffix and a full rechain all refuse — plus mandatory reason and authority fields, so a break excused by four hash values alone is not excused at all. Six fixtures replay his counterexamples. What remains open: a row appended since the last commit is not covered by the anchor, and the register lives in the repository it protects.</small></td><td>repairable by supersession</td><td><span class="tag w">partly applied</span></td></tr><tr><td>tools/tests/test_executive_log.py<br><small>test_max_actions_is_enforced_not_merely_recorded was vacuous twice over — it counted against the real action log, and its success branch passed when require() did NOT refuse. Rewritten against an isolated log with both branches asserted.</small></td><td>repairable by supersession</td><td><span class="tag g">verified</span></td></tr><tr><td>tools/codex_call.py<br><small>Caught LeaseExpired by name, so a refusal on the action bound or on unreadable evidence would have escaped as a traceback instead of an attested refusal. Now catches LeaseRefused.</small></td><td>repairable by supersession</td><td><span class="tag g">verified</span></td></tr><tr><td>tools/tests/test_lease_bounds.py<br><small>Codex on the first version: absence of the sentinel &#x27;mostly proves ordinary Python sequencing — a raised exception prevents the next statement&#x27;. True. It does not exercise a real caller&#x27;s catches, its refusal logging, or its subprocess and filesystem effects. Widened to 48 checks including the six anchor counterexamples, a module loaded by path with tools/ off sys.path, three unusable timestamps, and a stale register entry; still not a real caller&#x27;s effect boundary, which is task #20 and a prospective control rather than a claim made here.</small></td><td>partly repairable</td><td><span class="tag w">partly applied</span></td></tr></table></div></article><article class="e" data-actor="actor_external_adversarial_reviewer" data-control="prospective_control_required_not_implemented"><h3><a href="artifacts/deficiencies.md">D-65 — A defect in the landing tool was published as reproduced, and had never been run</a><span class="tag d">required, not implemented</span><span class="tag d">classification not human-reviewed</span></h3><p class="meta"><b>First articulated:</b> an external reviewer, 2026-08-12 · <code>Codex&#x27;s design review of the D-64 repair, reconciling the reported symptom against the live land.py; confirmed by re-reading the session transcript for the invocation that was never made</code></p><p class="meta"><b>Forward control:</b> Nothing distinguishes a claim this record REPORTS AS OBSERVED from one derived by reading code. The prose gates check attribution of quotations (D-53) and dispositions of absence claims; neither asks whether a stated reproduction was ever run. A candidate control: a reproduction claim must cite the invocation that produced it.</p><div class="wrap"><table><tr><th>Affected object</th><th>Repairable?</th><th>Remediation</th></tr><tr><td>record/executive/COMPACTION-NOTE-2026-08-12.md<br><small>The false claim is retained in the tense it was written in, with the correction attached beneath it. Corrections attach; they do not edit.</small></td><td>repairable by supersession</td><td><span class="tag g">verified</span></td></tr><tr><td>commit 8d2e19d — its message<br><small>A pushed commit message cannot be corrected without rewriting history, which the custodian ruled against on 2026-08-11 (&#x27;do not rewrite history&#x27;, 90e7095). The correction therefore attaches in the record rather than in the message, and this entry is the pointer between them. land.py itself is NOT listed as an affected object: it was not defective, and saying so is the finding.</small></td><td>not repairable</td><td><span class="tag d">impossible</span></td></tr></table></div></article>
