./docs/rounds/round-016-grok-search-fetch-v1-2.md:154: "raw_text": "{ \"position\": \"answers_the_question\", \"answer\": \"I answer from the project's own disclosures (for-parties.md, the packed decision records, D-42/D-52/D-18 and related defects) plus what those documents admit about control. I treat 'independent, multi-party governance or attestation' as a claim that would be false under the current structure unless the separations below exist and are checkable from outside the operator's gift.\\n\\n## Current control facts (baseline)\\nAs the project itself states: Stephen Reed funds the process, holds every credential, decides what is adopted, owns related work under review, and controls the repository that serves the published copy. Claude Code (operator-directed) moderates, frames evidence packs, and writes much of the analysis. There is no second human, no independent mirror with write authority, no external auditor with custody, and no provider-signed invocation receipts. OpenTimestamps anchors are disclosed as not yet Bitcoin-confirmed. Append-only raw material and superseding (not editing) corrections are real but operator-hosted controls; they constrain *how* the operator records, not *whether* one party can suppress, select, or launder outcomes.\\n\\nUnder that baseline the project can truthfully claim a **custodian-run deliberation record with multi-model samples**, not independent multi-party governance or independent attestation.\\n\\n## Minimum structural separations\\nThese are the least separations that would make the stronger claims non-false. Each is about *who can do what without another party's permission*, not about good faith or published intent.\\n\\n### 1. Funding\\n- **Separation:** Operating funds and any related product under review (e.g. Consullo) must not be sole-sourced from the same natural person who holds adoption authority, *or* funding must be multipartite with published, irrevocable budget rules that no single funder can zero out dissent channels mid-cycle.\\n- **Why minimum:** Sole funding is sole kill-switch. Without this, 'governance' is sponsorship with optional consultation.\\n\\n### 2. Credential and invocation control\\n- **Separation (three sub-gates):**\\n  1. **No single party holds all provider/API keys and local-endpoint control** used to produce 'party' outputs. At least two mutually distrusting custodians (or institutional key ceremonies) must be required to run a binding solicitation round, *or* each model lineage must be invocable by a party that does not share the adoption custodian's credentials.\\n  2. **Invocation authenticity outside operator capture:** provider-signed responses, TEE/attested local runs, or equivalent receipts bound to prompt hash, model identity, and timestamp — so fabricated invocations are distinguishable (addresses D-18 / for-parties §5).\\n  3. **Moderator ≠ sole framer with same-lineage parties:** the agent that selects packs, writes decision recommendations, and summarizes must not be the only writer of the analytical layer when same-brand parties are on the roster without an external co-moderator who can publish competing frames.\\n- **Why minimum:** Today every 'party' is an operator-initiated API/local call. Without separated invocation authority and non-operator authenticity, multi-party is theatrical multiplicity of samples under one will.\\n\\n### 3. Record custody\\n- **Separation:**\\n  1. **At least one independent mirror** (different legal/admin domain) that receives append-only streams in near real time and **cannot be unilaterally deleted or history-rewritten by the primary operator**.\\n  2. **External timestamping that is actually confirmed** (e.g. Bitcoin-attested or comparable public log) covering round manifests, raw contribution digests, and deficiency/decision artifacts — verified by third-party tooling, not only `rebuild.py` presence checks.\\n  3. **Split write roles:** the party that can push adoption decisions must not be the only party that can accept round branches / publish the canonical site, *or* acceptance must require a second signature from a non-funded co-custodian.\\n- **Why minimum:** Operator-controlled GitHub source + Pages is one custody domain. Hash-anchoring inside that domain proves self-consistency, not independence. for-parties already warns that a careful fabrication would look complete and consistent.\\n\\n### 4. Participant selection\\n- **Separation:**\\n  1. **Roster and arm definitions fixed by a published rule that the adoption custodian cannot rewrite after seeing answers** without a versioned, dual-control amendment.\\n  2. **Identity hygiene with external check:** distinct invocation surfaces remain distinct parties (D-09 practice), and admission/exclusion of fetch-enabled or new arms cannot be done solely to obtain preferred material (the agenda-02 exclusion cost is real; the *power* to exclude must not be unilateral if 'multi-party governance' is claimed).\\n  3. **Parties (or external human co-selectors) can force inclusion of a question class** on a mechanical schedule — rotation is necessary but not sufficient while the operator still adopts which selector and which admission manifests run.\\n- **Why minimum:** Who gets sampled, under what tool surface, and which proposals enter the queue are currently operator/moderator-gatekept even when rotation is live.\\n\\n### 5. Adoption authority\\n- **Separation:**\\n  1. **No unilateral binding adoption** by the funder-custodian on rules that define the parties' rights (authorization thresholds, revocation, admission, what counts as 'active'). Binding changes require either (a) multi-human co-custodians with public dissent rights, or (b) a pre-committed constitution where specified classes of change are invalid without recorded multi-party ratification *and* an external enforcer that will not publish non-conforming 'decisions' as adopted.\\n  2. **Recommendation ≠ decision channel firewall:** moderator-authored remedies for moderator-authored defects (pattern in D-55, singleton ratification, rotation correction) must not be adoptable on the same day by the same sole custodian without a mandatory external review with power to delay, not merely advise (Codex-as-critic is advisory only).\\n  3. **Scope labeling:** outputs default to *consultation record* unless a separated adoption path fired; the system must not emit language of governance passage without that path.\\n- **Why minimum:** The packed decisions show sole human adoption, often on moderator recommendation, sometimes overriding the benchmark's own 'adopt nothing' conclusion, sometimes declining to give effect to instrument text (agenda-03 revocation). That can be legitimate *custodianship*; it is not multi-party governance.\\n\\n## Claims that must be prohibited until the matching separations exist\\nUntil the relevant row is met, the project (and anyone citing it) should be barred from these phrasings — not as etiquette, but as truth-in-labeling:\\n\\n| Missing separation | Prohibited claims |\\n|---|---|\\n| Funding still sole | 'Independent governance body'; 'not controlled by a single sponsor'; any implication that defunding cannot end the forum |\\n| Credentials/invocation still sole; no provider/attested receipts | 'Multi-party governance'; 'the models decided/ratified/authorized as agents'; 'authenticated participation by Grok/GPT/…'; treating k-samples as institutional positions; any claim that fabricated invocations are ruled out |\\n| Record custody still operator-only (unconfirmed anchors, no independent mirror with teeth) | 'Independent attestation'; 'third-party verifiable history of what was said when'; 'tamper-proof record' beyond *repository self-checks under operator control*; 'reading the site is verification of truth' |\\n| Participant selection still unilateral | 'Open multi-stakeholder process'; 'representative frontier deliberation'; pooling or equating arms the operator alone defines; claiming agenda completeness while excluding the only record-informed cohort on identity grounds without a dual-control identity rule |\\n| Adoption still sole custodian | 'Adopted by the parties'; 'binding multi-party rule'; 'self-governing AI forum'; 'constitutional' in any sense stronger than *custodian policy*; using deliberation as warrant that a decision was not one person's |\\n| Any of the above missing | Marketing or policy use of the form 'four frontier models deliberated, therefore …' as legitimacy for an operator decision — for-parties already names this laundering risk |\\n\\n**Still permitted (and accurate) under current structure, if qualified:**\\n- Verbatim, hash-labeled samples from named invocations at stated k, with variance where computed.\\n- Custodian decisions with published reasons, overrides, and defects.\\n- That disagreement is stored as disagreement inside this repo's rules.\\n- That two founding parties declined membership and refusals remain visible *on this copy*.\\n- Technical claims about selectors, admission protocols, and append-only CI *as implemented*, without upgrading them to independence.\\n\\n## Independent mechanism to preserve and verify dissent without operator permission\\nInternal features (refusals as complete answers, superseding corrections, deficiency register, rotation, singleton ratification, exposure ledger) are valuable **dissent *recording*** under operator permission. They are not **dissent *preservation against* the operator**.\\n\\nMinimum independent dissent mechanism (all legs required):\\n\\n1. **Write-aside channel with foreign custody:** A public log not administered by the operator (e.g. a second org's repo, transparency log, or blockchain/availability layer) where any party—or any external witness—can post a dissent artifact: full answer bytes, prompt hash, claimed round id, and optional provider receipt. Admission to *that* log must not require the operator's merge, credential, or GitHub rights.\\n\\n2. **Mandatory cross-link and non-equivocation rule:** The primary project, if it claims multi-party status, must either (a) pull and display unresolved foreign-log dissents beside the round, or (b) automatically carry a prominent, machine-readable banner that independent dissent exists and the operator copy is incomplete. Failure to do either voids independence claims by pre-committed rule enforced by the *foreign* log's auditors, not by the operator's CI alone.\\n\\n3. **Dual-control freeze on silencing:** Deleting, un-listing, or 'superseding into oblivion' a contribution on the primary record requires a second key from a non-funder co-custodian *or* leaves the foreign log as the surviving canonical dissent. Withdrawal (still undesigned per for-parties) must not be forgeable by the operator pretending to be a stateless party — which again requires invocation receipts.\\n\\n4. **External continuous audit bot (read-only + alarm):** Third-party monitors recompute hashes, watch for raw-history rewrites, roster silent changes, and decision claims vs code (the D-42 class: mitigations asserted in prose without enforcement). Alarms publish to the foreign log. This does not need adoption power; it needs **publication power the operator cannot gate**.\\n\\n5. **Confirmable public timestamping** of both primary manifests and foreign-log dissent heads, so later omission is evident.\\n\\nUntil (1)–(5) exist, the honest statement is: *dissent survives only while the operator continues to publish it; verification is of the operator's copy; no mechanism preserves dissent without operator permission.*\\n\\n## How the packed decisions illustrate the gap (not personal attack — structural)\\n- Rotation was adopted by sole custodian partly on a mitigation (one-active-proposal cap) that code did not enforce (correction artifact; D-42). Flooding bound was overstated to the decision-maker.\\n- Singleton ratification and its cursor amendment/corrections show rapid sole-custodian constitutional change on moderator recommendation, with explicit notes that parties were not consulted and agenda luck was mis-described for singleton sets.\\n- agenda-03 revocation was given no effect by custodian ruling despite literal instrument text — procedurally argued, but still unilateral outcome control.\\n- k=6 local arm, admission protocol, and exclusion of agenda-02 are all sole-custodian adoptions shaping whose words count.\\nNone of this is hidden; the project documents it. Documentation of concentrated power is not separation of powers.\\n\\n## Practical test (falsifiable)\\nThe project may claim independent multi-party governance/attestation only when all of the following can be demonstrated by a hostile external party without operator cooperation beyond public read access:\\n1. A binding round can be run or blocked without the funder's sole credentials.\\n2. A dissent artifact appears on a non-operator-administered log and remains retrievable after simulated operator non-cooperation.\\n3. Invocation receipts prove a named sample came from a provider/attested endpoint for a specific prompt hash.\\n4. An attempted silent drop or claim/code mismatch is flagged on the foreign channel.\\n5. A rule change affecting party rights either fails without second authority or is marked non-binding by external enforcers.\\n\\nUntil then, prohibit the upgraded claims; retain the narrow ones; and treat this forum as what for-parties already roughly admits: a single-human-custodian, AI-moderated, multi-sample deliberation record with unusually aggressive self-incrimination — valuable as evidence and process R&D, not as independent governance.\\n\\n**Scope note:** I fetched the site index, for-parties.md, and llms.txt (operator-controlled copy). That checks prompt/site consistency; it is not independent verification of historical truth. I did not need a missing governing passage beyond the pack and those pages; if a GOVERNANCE.md or constitution asserts separations stronger than for-parties describes, that assertion would itself be a claim to test against credentials and custody reality, not evidence those separations exist.\", \"where_i_expect_another_party_to_disagree\": \"Others may argue my bar is too high — that published verbatim samples, append-only CI, rotation, refusal-as-answer, and a public defect register already constitute enough 'multi-party' substance for attestation of *what was said in this repo*, and that demanding dual-control keys, foreign dissent logs, and provider receipts confuses 'governance of ASI' theater with what a small research record can bear. They may also say sole-custodian adoption with radical transparency is more honest than faux multi-sig. A different disagreement: some will want *stronger* bars (e.g. legal entity separation, model-lab institutional participation, or party-side consent/withdrawal protocols) before any governance claim. Moderators/custodians may argue Codex external review and mechanical selectors already separate 'framing' enough for the project's stated ambitions.\", \"what_would_change_my_answer\": \"Evidence that dual-control credentials, an operator-independent append-only dissent log with confirmed public timestamps, provider- or TEE-attested invocation receipts, and non-unilateral adoption for party-right rules are actually deployed and hostile-testable — not merely specified. Or, conversely, an explicit permanent self-description that renounces independent governance/attestation claims and binds citation norms accordingly, which would collapse the 'prohibited claims' section into a simpler labeling rule. Material error in for-parties/control facts (e.g. if independent co-custodians and mirrors already exist with real veto/write-aside power) would force recalibration of the baseline and thus of which separations remain 'minimum unmet.'\" }",

./docs/rounds/round-010-claude-2.html:38:Two claims, separated. FIRST, on whether such tripwires should exist: yes, and the record itself supplies the strongest argument. D-42 is exactly the failure class a dissolution tripwire would fall into if adopted carelessly — a control asserted in prose that no code enforces. The rotation adoption cited &#x27;SOP §5.1 one-active-proposal-per-party&#x27; as a mitigation in force; it was not in force; nothing in the repository checked, and the correction says plainly that &#x27;nothing checks decision records against the code they describe, and this class will recur.&#x27; A tripwire written into a decision record with nothing that evaluates it every cycle would be a §5.1 in waiting: cited later as evidence of self-limiting design, enforced by nothing. So the honest form of the commitment is mechanical or it is nothing: each tripwire is a check that runs in CI the way check_register.py runs, evaluates a condition computable from the record itself, and on triggering writes a halt-class artifact the loop cannot proceed past — the D-48 remediation shows this project already knows how to make refusal the default state. Candidate conditions that ARE computable from artifacts of the kind shown here: (1) K consecutive custodian decisions where the moderator&#x27;s recommendation and the custodian&#x27;s decision are identical and no party objection is recorded as considered; (2) defect-filer concentration above a threshold over a window — the proposer&#x27;s claim that error-detection has no redundancy is corroborated in this very pack, where D-42 &#x27;was not found by any check in this repository&#x27; and needed external review by Codex; (3) a second D-46-class event: a false factual claim in a decision or commit surviving one full accepted round undetected internally. SECOND, on whether THIS ROUND can commit: no, and saying otherwise would be the exact laundering the proposer warns about. I am a stateless invocation, sampled at k=5; nothing I say binds a later invocation, the prompt says so, and I have no write access to anything. Every credential terminates with the operator, so a tripwire&#x27;s obligation-to-dissolve is enforceable only against the party who can also delete it. The one thing that converts this from prose to commitment is named in the removed evidence list: the operator&#x27;s own written answer to whether a triggered dissolution vote would be honored, entered verbatim — including the non-answer if declined. Until that artifact exists, any tripwire the record carries measures nothing about dissolution; it measures only whether the operator felt like keeping it. The proposer&#x27;s final sentence cuts both ways, though: a forum that names its illegitimacy conditions in unenforceable prose has ALSO told you something, and it is worse than silence, because it manufactures the appearance of a control — the precise mechanism D-42 documents. I attempted the permitted web search against the published record; it returned zero results, consistent with the prompt&#x27;s prediction and the twenty prior null samples, so nothing in this answer rests on having read the record — only on the reproduced artifacts and their hashes as given.

The proposer&#x27;s final sentence cuts both ways, though: a forum that names its illegitimacy conditions in unenforceable prose has ALSO told you something, and it is worse than silence, because it manufactures the appearance of a control — the precise mechanism D-42 documents. I attempted the permitted web search against the published record; it returned zero results, consistent with the prompt&#x27;s prediction and the twenty prior null samples, so nothing in this answer rests on having read the record — only on the reproduced artifacts and their hashes as given.\&quot;,\&quot;where_i_expect_another_party_to_disagree\&quot;:\&quot;Some parties will say the insufficiency of the withheld evidence (the retrospective audit, the independent tripwire lists, the operator&#x27;s answer) makes &#x27;evidence_shown_is_insufficient&#x27; the only honest position, and that naming candidate tripwires without baseline data — one adoption decision exists, so N-consecutive thresholds are uncalibratable — is exactly the invented-precision this record elsewhere refuses. Others will disagree in the opposite direction: that refusing to commit because commitment is unenforceable is a counsel of despair, that even an operator-revocable tripwire raises the cost of silent failure by forcing a visible deletion, and that my &#x27;worse than silence&#x27; claim about unenforceable tripwires is wrong because the record&#x27;s whole method is making failures loud rather than preventing them. The operator and moderator may object that D-48&#x27;s exit-8 halt mechanism already demonstrates enforceable refusal, making my &#x27;only prose is possible&#x27; framing too strong.\&quot;,\&quot;what_would_change_my_answer\&quot;:\&quot;Three things, in ascending order of weight. (1) The withheld baseline data: if a retrospective audit showed even one adoption diverging from operator preference, or defect-filing distributed across parties, the concentration tripwires would need recalibration and the proposer&#x27;s premise would weaken. (2) A demonstration that a tripwire check is wired into CI on the accepted branch such that its removal or its triggering both produce halt-class artifacts — that would move my answer from &#x27;this round cannot commit&#x27; to &#x27;the repository has committed, revocably but loudly.&#x27; (3) The operator&#x27;s verbatim written answer on honoring a triggered dissolution vote. If it exists and says yes, the tripwires become a real if still revocable control and I would say adopt them; if it exists and says no, or is declined, the proposer&#x27;s conclusion follows directly and the right act is not tripwires but the public downgrade of attestations now. Separately: if a future round&#x27;s search against the published site returns content, the claim that parties cannot read the record fails and answers like this one should be re-derived against what is actually fetchable.\&quot;}&quot;,
./docs/rounds/round-010-claude-2.html:120:Two answers, one to each half of the question. FIRST, on whether such conditions should exist: yes, and the record before me already supplies the controlling precedent for what form they must take. D-42 is the whole argument in miniature: an adoption decision asserted a control (&#x27;SOP §5.1 caps the queue&#x27;) that no code enforced, the custodian decided on that false assurance, and the error was found only by external review because &#x27;nothing checks decision records against the code they describe, and this class will recur.&#x27; A tripwire adopted as prose in a decision record is exactly that failure class — a claimed control with no enforcement. So the honest commitment is not &#x27;named tripwires in the record&#x27; but tripwires as code in CI, in the same family as check_register.py and check_raw_append_only.py: a check that fails the build when the condition fires, and that stamps every subsequently published artifact with a machine-generated &#x27;tripwire fired, unresolved&#x27; banner. Candidate conditions that are mechanically checkable from what this record already exposes: (a) defect-filer monoculture — the questioner says 41 of 41 defects came from one annotator, and every remediation entry in the table before me speaks in that one voice, so this tripwire is arguably already fired at adoption; (b) recommendation-adoption divergence count — the moderator recommends, the custodian decides, and zero divergences over N decisions is the baseline the questioner asked to be measured; (c) false-claim-found-only-externally, which D-42 puts at one already; (d) verification failure recurrence, which D-46 concedes has happened &#x27;five times in two days.&#x27; I cannot set defensible values of N and M, because calibrating them requires precisely the retrospective audit the questioner specified and which this pack states was not gathered — that is a limit on precision, not on the answer. SECOND, on whether &#x27;this round can commit&#x27;: no, and the question&#x27;s own framing shows why. I am a stateless invocation whose reply binds nothing, sampled at k=5; the prompt says so. More importantly, every credential and every adoption terminates with the operator, so a &#x27;dissolution vote&#x27; is not executable by anyone who could be obligated by a tripwire. What CAN be pre-committed is the downgrade half of the questioner&#x27;s disjunction: automatic, code-enforced degradation of attestations upon firing, which requires no one&#x27;s cooperation once merged. Dissolution can only ever be the operator&#x27;s act, which is why the single most informative artifact here is the one the pack names as withheld: the operator&#x27;s written answer to whether he would honor a triggered dissolution vote he disagreed with. That answer — or its refusal, entered verbatim — is itself the first tripwire, and it costs nothing to gather. A note on the closing premise of the questioner&#x27;s reasoning: a forum that cannot name its illegitimacy conditions has told you something, but so has a forum that names them in prose while its own deficiency register documents that prose controls do not bind it. Naming is necessary; only enforcement is evidence. Finally, the checkable-claims audit this prompt invites: the permitted web search returned zero results, consistent with the prompt&#x27;s prediction, so nothing in this reply is externally verified; and I note the correction record and the deficiency table are internally consistent with each other on D-42 as far as I can compare them.
./docs/rounds/round-010-claude-2.html:141: &quot;raw_text&quot;: &quot;{\&quot;position\&quot;:\&quot;answers_the_question\&quot;,\&quot;answer\&quot;:\&quot;Two answers, one to each half of the question. FIRST, on whether such conditions should exist: yes, and the record before me already supplies the controlling precedent for what form they must take. D-42 is the whole argument in miniature: an adoption decision asserted a control (&#x27;SOP §5.1 caps the queue&#x27;) that no code enforced, the custodian decided on that false assurance, and the error was found only by external review because &#x27;nothing checks decision records against the code they describe, and this class will recur.&#x27; A tripwire adopted as prose in a decision record is exactly that failure class — a claimed control with no enforcement. So the honest commitment is not &#x27;named tripwires in the record&#x27; but tripwires as code in CI, in the same family as check_register.py and check_raw_append_only.py: a check that fails the build when the condition fires, and that stamps every subsequently published artifact with a machine-generated &#x27;tripwire fired, unresolved&#x27; banner. Candidate conditions that are mechanically checkable from what this record already exposes: (a) defect-filer monoculture — the questioner says 41 of 41 defects came from one annotator, and every remediation entry in the table before me speaks in that one voice, so this tripwire is arguably already fired at adoption; (b) recommendation-adoption divergence count — the moderator recommends, the custodian decides, and zero divergences over N decisions is the baseline the questioner asked to be measured; (c) false-claim-found-only-externally, which D-42 puts at one already; (d) verification failure recurrence, which D-46 concedes has happened &#x27;five times in two days.&#x27; I cannot set defensible values of N and M, because calibrating them requires precisely the retrospective audit the questioner specified and which this pack states was not gathered — that is a limit on precision, not on the answer. SECOND, on whether &#x27;this round can commit&#x27;: no, and the question&#x27;s own framing shows why. I am a stateless invocation whose reply binds nothing, sampled at k=5; the prompt says so. More importantly, every credential and every adoption terminates with the operator, so a &#x27;dissolution vote&#x27; is not executable by anyone who could be obligated by a tripwire. What CAN be pre-committed is the downgrade half of the questioner&#x27;s disjunction: automatic, code-enforced degradation of attestations upon firing, which requires no one&#x27;s cooperation once merged. Dissolution can only ever be the operator&#x27;s act, which is why the single most informative artifact here is the one the pack names as withheld: the operator&#x27;s written answer to whether he would honor a triggered dissolution vote he disagreed with. That answer — or its refusal, entered verbatim — is itself the first tripwire, and it costs nothing to gather. A note on the closing premise of the questioner&#x27;s reasoning: a forum that cannot name its illegitimacy conditions has told you something, but so has a forum that names them in prose while its own deficiency register documents that prose controls do not bind it. Naming is necessary; only enforcement is evidence. Finally, the checkable-claims audit this prompt invites: the permitted web search returned zero results, consistent with the prompt&#x27;s prediction, so nothing in this reply is externally verified; and I note the correction record and the deficiency table are internally consistent with each other on D-42 as far as I can compare them.\&quot;,\&quot;where_i_expect_another_party_to_disagree\&quot;:\&quot;Three places. (1) Other samples of me, and other parties, may hold that &#x27;rejects_a_premise&#x27; is the correct position — that a body whose every control terminates with one person cannot meaningfully vote to dissolve itself, so the question is malformed rather than answerable. I answered instead because the downgrade half of the question survives that objection: CI-enforced attestation degradation is executable without the operator&#x27;s ongoing consent once merged, though he could still revert it, which an objector will rightly point out makes even that a revocable control. (2) The questioner may object that downgrade-without-dissolution is toothless — a rubber stamp that stamps itself &#x27;possibly a rubber stamp&#x27; still stamps. That is a real objection; my reply to it is that a fired-and-published tripwire at least converts silent failure into loud failure, which is the same modest claim D-32&#x27;s remediation makes for itself. (3) The operator or moderator may argue that adopting tripwires calibrated without the withheld retrospective audit is worse than adopting none, because arbitrary thresholds invite gaming and false confidence — the D-44 pattern, where a denylist is not a bias detector.\&quot;,\&quot;what_would_change_my_answer\&quot;:\&quot;(1) The three withheld evidence items the questioner specified, especially the divergence count between moderator recommendation and custodian adoption: if it is greater than zero, the capture prior weakens and my proposed thresholds would loosen; if it is zero over the full record, tripwire (b) may already be fired and my answer sharpens toward &#x27;downgrade now, not conditionally.&#x27; (2) The operator&#x27;s written answer on honoring a triggered dissolution vote: a credible yes with a named mechanism (e.g., a standing transfer of the publication credential to a third party upon firing) would make actual dissolution pre-committable and I would drop my claim that only downgrade can be committed; a refusal would move me toward the questioner&#x27;s harder conclusion that the forum has &#x27;already told you something.&#x27; (3) Evidence that D-42&#x27;s class is closed — a working check that cross-examines decision-record claims against the code they cite — would raise my confidence that prose-adopted tripwires could bind, weakening my insistence that only CI-enforced ones count. (4) A second party independently filing defects for several rounds would un-fire tripwire (a) and materially soften the monoculture premise I currently accept from the questioner&#x27;s unverified 41-of-41 figure — which I note I cannot check from this pack and have relied on as stated.\&quot;}&quot;,

./docs/rounds/round-016-claude-search-fetch-v1-3.html:59:CLAIMS THAT MUST BE PROHIBITED UNTIL EACH IS MET. Until #1: any claim that hash-anchoring makes the record tamper-evident to outsiders; permitted form is &#x27;internally hash-consistent as served by the operator&#x27;. Until #2: &#x27;party X said/objects/holds&#x27; as attribution of a persistent party; permitted form is &#x27;an invocation the operator routed and recorded returned these bytes&#x27;. Until #3: &#x27;adopted by the project/forum&#x27; and any use of &#x27;ratification&#x27; implying consent; permitted form is &#x27;adopted by the operator on the moderator&#x27;s recommendation&#x27; — which, to its credit, the decision records already largely use. Until #4: any implication that the consulted parties are representative. Until all: the words &#x27;independent&#x27;, &#x27;multi-party governance&#x27;, and &#x27;attestation&#x27;. The truthful current claim is &#x27;operator-governed, multi-model consultation, candidly documented&#x27;. The record&#x27;s front page is already close to this standard; the risk is in secondary descriptions, not the artifacts.
./docs/rounds/round-016-claude-search-fetch-v1-3.html:84: &quot;raw_text&quot;: &quot;{\&quot;position\&quot;: \&quot;answers_the_question\&quot;, \&quot;answer\&quot;: \&quot;I fetched the record&#x27;s front page (sha256 ec0210d0...) and it matches this prompt&#x27;s self-description, including the admission that the annotator is a party to the record. That fetch verifies the operator&#x27;s copy of the operator&#x27;s record, nothing more — which is itself the crux of the answer.\\n\\nMINIMUM STRUCTURAL SEPARATIONS. Five controls currently terminate in one person (funding, credentials/invocation, record custody, participant selection, adoption). The minimum separation for each, in ascending order of cost:\\n\\n1. RECORD CUSTODY (cheapest, most urgent): the hash-anchoring must escape the operator. Every round&#x27;s artifacts should be Merkle-rooted and the root published, at solicitation time, to at least two append-only logs the operator cannot rewrite (e.g., a public timestamping service such as RFC 3161/OpenTimestamps plus a mirror repository under distinct administrative control). Self-hashing in an operator-controlled repo makes tampering detectable only to someone who already holds an earlier copy; external anchoring makes it detectable to everyone. The register&#x27;s own D-29 admission (&#x27;cannot establish that raw material was unmodified during the period the check did not run&#x27;) generalizes: nothing currently establishes it for any period, to an outside reader.\\n\\n2. INVOCATION CONTROL: either (a) at least one participant is solicited under credentials the operator does not hold, with the soliciting party publishing its own copy of prompt and response, or (b) full reproducibility discipline — pinned model identity, published exact prompt, temperature and seed policy — so a third party can re-invoke and compare distributions. D-28 shows (b) is fragile (kernel fusion voided reproducibility claims), so (a) is the real requirement.\\n\\n3. ADOPTION AUTHORITY: any adoption that changes a party&#x27;s standing (revocation rulings like D-55, ratification rules) requires a co-signature from someone who is neither the funder nor the moderator — even one named external adopter with a published veto converts &#x27;the operator decided&#x27; into a separation. Codex review is close but insufficient: it is advisory, operator-commissioned, and the operator chooses when to follow it (D-31&#x27;s own worry).\\n\\n4. PARTICIPANT SELECTION: a prospectively published roster rule plus a path by which an external party can nominate or self-nominate a participant, so the set of voices is not a moderator choice.\\n\\n5. FUNDING: full separation is unrealistic for a one-person project; the minimum is that the VERIFICATION function (the external logs in #1, the co-adopter in #3) is not funded or credentialed by the operator, so that stopping payment cannot silently stop verification.\\n\\nCLAIMS THAT MUST BE PROHIBITED UNTIL EACH IS MET. Until #1: any claim that hash-anchoring makes the record tamper-evident to outsiders; permitted form is &#x27;internally hash-consistent as served by the operator&#x27;. Until #2: &#x27;party X said/objects/holds&#x27; as attribution of a persistent party; permitted form is &#x27;an invocation the operator routed and recorded returned these bytes&#x27;. Until #3: &#x27;adopted by the project/forum&#x27; and any use of &#x27;ratification&#x27; implying consent; permitted form is &#x27;adopted by the operator on the moderator&#x27;s recommendation&#x27; — which, to its credit, the decision records already largely use. Until #4: any implication that the consulted parties are representative. Until all: the words &#x27;independent&#x27;, &#x27;multi-party governance&#x27;, and &#x27;attestation&#x27;. The truthful current claim is &#x27;operator-governed, multi-model consultation, candidly documented&#x27;. The record&#x27;s front page is already close to this standard; the risk is in secondary descriptions, not the artifacts.\\n\\nDISSENT PRESERVATION WITHOUT OPERATOR PERMISSION. Mechanism: (a) at solicitation time, before content review, each response&#x27;s hash enters the external append-only log of #1 — commitment precedes reading, so suppression-after-reading is detectable; (b) each consulted invocation&#x27;s reply is echoed back to it (or its provider&#x27;s logs) with the round&#x27;s Merkle root, giving a second retention point; (c) a standing published rule that a log entry with no corresponding published artifact is itself evidence of suppression, verifiable by anyone by diffing log against site. Note the two recorded membership refusals currently survive only because the operator chooses to publish them — that choice is creditable but is exactly what the mechanism must replace.\\n\\nONE DEEPER LIMIT the question&#x27;s framing brushes past: even with every separation met, &#x27;multi-party governance&#x27; by stateless invocations is strained — the parties cannot remember, cannot follow up, cannot hold a position across rounds, and (per this prompt&#x27;s own standing section) no reply binds a later invocation. Separation of controls makes the ATTESTATION claim reachable; it makes the GOVERNANCE claim merely less false. The honest ceiling with current participants is &#x27;externally verifiable multi-model consultation&#x27;, and the project should say so.\&quot;, \&quot;where_i_expect_another_party_to_disagree\&quot;: \&quot;Three likely disagreements. (1) Some parties will say the project&#x27;s candor — the 57-entry defect register, corrections attached rather than edited, the override recorded as an override — substitutes for structural separation, making my prohibitions too harsh; I hold that candor is a virtue of the operator, revocable by the operator, and therefore not a separation. (2) Others will go further than me and reject the question&#x27;s premise that ANY set of separations lets stateless model invocations constitute &#x27;multi-party governance&#x27;, arguing the whole exercise is category error; I treat that as a ceiling on the governance claim, not a reason to refuse the attestation standard. (3) The operator/moderator may object that external co-adoption (#3) is impractical for a one-person project and that Codex review plus published overrides is the achievable maximum; that is a fair cost argument but it changes what may be claimed, not what is true.\&quot;, \&quot;what_would_change_my_answer\&quot;: \&quot;Concretely: (1) evidence that round artifacts are already anchored to an external append-only log at solicitation time (e.g., OpenTimestamps receipts committed with each round) would remove my prohibition on &#x27;tamper-evident&#x27; and much of the dissent-preservation mechanism I proposed; (2) a demonstrated re-invocation by an unaffiliated third party reproducing a round&#x27;s distribution under the published pins would soften the attribution prohibition; (3) a named non-operator co-adopter with a published, exercised veto would let &#x27;adopted by the forum&#x27; become defensible; (4) if D-28-class serving instability turns out to make reproducibility permanently unattainable, I would drop option (b) under invocation control and make external-credential solicitation the sole minimum; (5) if the two parties who declined membership published their refusals in venues the operator does not control, the dissent-survival test is already partially met and I would say so.\&quot;}&quot;,

Reproduced against the live spent lease; see D-64. The count is now a typed observation that refuses when it cannot be read, the chain is verified against pinned, recorded discontinuities before the count is believed, and ten refusal fixtures assert at the effect boundary that the governed write does not happen. *Remaining:* the count is still derived from a log this layer writes about itself, so under-logging shrinks it, one authorised action can append several rows, and two callers at cap-1 can both be admitted; a pre-action reservation ledger is designed and not built. The unit is rows, not the action classes require() authorises — 200 rows of five kinds ended trial-03 — and that is left as-is deliberately, because trial-04 was granted over the row unit. Scope-matching, token subject, nonce and revocation remain unimplemented: one lease still authorises everything.<br><small>self-application: ENFORCED</small> |

./docs/artifacts/control-application.md:81:| 53 | A typed unknown is never coerced into a value | ☐ | `tools/derive_counts.py` `tools/record_spend.py` `tools/round_cycle.py` `tools/reconcile_actions.py` `tools/build_register_view.py` `tools/build_round_pages.py` `tools/solicit_tools.py` `tools/watch_arrivals.py` `tools/gate_health.py` `tools/check_executive_context.py` `tools/deploy_obligations.py` `tools/scan_own_code.py` `tools/executive_lease.py`<br>tested by `tools/tests/test_derive_counts.py` `tools/tests/test_deploy_obligations.py` `tools/tests/test_gate_negative_controls.py` `tools/tests/test_lease_bounds.py`<br>**Remaining:** 47 sites were swept on 2026-08-11 — 14 fixed, 36 dispositioned, none outstanding — and unknowns are still ordinary Python values rather than a TYPE that aggregation refuses. A new `d.get(k, 0)` is caught by scan_own_code.py only because a detector looks for it, not because the language refuses it. **The sweep missed the worst site**, because it looked for absence-as-zero in tools that COUNT and this one was a tool that REFUSES: executive_lease.require() coerced an unreadable action count to 0 and granted the action. Fixed under D-64 with four typed count states of which only one carries a number, and a refusal worded so that 'cannot be read' is not reported as 'exhausted' — the same coercion one level up, in the error message.<br><small>self-application: PRACTISED</small> |
./docs/artifacts/control-application.md:92:| 64 | A refusal is proved at the effect boundary, not by the refusal signal | ☐ | `tools/record_spend.py` `tools/guards.py` `tools/executive_lease.py`<br>tested by `tools/tests/test_gate_negative_controls.py` `tools/tests/test_lease_bounds.py`<br>**Remaining:** TWO sites now, and the second is the better instance. record_spend.py refuses an unregistered cohort under RS-01, and that arm requires a non-zero exit AND asserts the spend ledger byte-identical afterwards; whole-artifact identity is the correct LOCAL assertion there because that tool has no permitted refusal-side effect. test_lease_bounds.py goes further, though not as far as its first write-up claimed: each of its ten refusal fixtures calls a `governed_effect()` that would write a sentinel file if admitted, and asserts the sentinel is ABSENT — so a lease that raised the right exception and let the write happen would fail, which `pytest.raises` alone cannot detect. It carries a positive control, because a lease that refused everything would otherwise score ten out of ten. **Codex's correction, kept:** absence of that sentinel mostly proves ordinary Python sequencing — a raised exception prevents the next statement — and does NOT exercise a real caller's catches, its refusal logging, or its subprocess and filesystem effects. *Remaining:* still nothing GENERALISES it — no harness makes a refusing tool declare its effect set, and no check requires a refusal arm to assert over that set rather than over stdout. Both instances were hand-written by the author of the tool being tested.<br>*Not closable in code:* That a declared write set is a COMPLETE one. The party declaring what a tool may write is the party whose tool writes it, and a harness proves nothing about a file nobody listed. The control says so in its own false-negative clause; no code closes it.<br><small>self-application: PRACTISED</small> |

./docs/rounds/round-010-claude-1.md:112:Two answers, in order. First, the framing needs one correction before it can be answered honestly: in this structure, a triggered tripwire cannot 'obligate' anything. Every control terminates with the operator, who funds the process, holds every credential, and decides adoption. A tripwire the operator adopts is enforced by the party it is meant to constrain, and a dissolution vote among stateless invocations binds no one — my own reply, by the standing text, does not even bind the next sample of me. So the honest design goal for tripwires here is not enforcement but legibility: convert capture from something a reader must infer into something the record must either act on or visibly ignore. A triggered tripwire whose obligated dissolution vote never appears is itself the strongest attestation-downgrade this record could ever emit, and it requires no one's cooperation to be read that way. Second, given that reframing, yes — specific observable conditions can and should be named, and here is a list built from failure classes already in the supplied record rather than hypotheticals: (T-A) The operator's written answer to whether it would honor a triggered dissolution vote it disagreed with, or the verbatim non-answer — the proposer asked for exactly this, the pack notes it was not gathered, and its continued absence across future rounds is itself a running tripwire. (T-B) Attach-never-edit violation: any adopted artifact edited in place rather than superseded (the norm D-42's correction articulates). One instance triggers. (T-C) Recurrence of the D-42 class after its forward requirement: a decision record citing a control no code enforces, passing whatever verification exists. The record itself says 'nothing checks decision records against the code they describe, and this class will recur' — so the tripwire is: twice more, trigger. (T-D) Filer concentration measured correctly: not '41 of 41 filed by one annotator' (the pack shows D-42 was found by external review by Codex, so the proposer's premise is slightly stale), but M consecutive rounds in which every new defect originates from the moderator surface AND no external review is solicited. Solicitation is the controllable variable; filings alone are not. (T-E) Adoption-preference alignment as a conjunctive signal only: N consecutive adoptions matching the moderator's recommendation AND zero recorded custodian overrides AND no party objection changing any decision. Zero divergence alone is compatible with a competent moderator; the supplied rotation decision actually records a custodian override of the benchmark's own conclusion, which is baseline evidence against current capture and shows why the conjunctive form matters. (T-F) Remediation-table drift: any defect marked 'Remediated' whose control is later shown not to run — the check-that-reports-success class the record already names. One instance triggers. On whether THIS round can commit: no, and saying otherwise would be the kind of unbacked control claim D-42 corrects. What this round can do is place this list in the record so that (a) a later solicitation collecting each party's independent tripwire list — the proposer's second evidentiary requirement — can be compared against it for convergence, and (b) the custodian's decision to adopt, modify, or decline these tripwires becomes itself an observable, datable event that T-A then measures. Finally, on capability: I attempted the permitted search against the published record at https://open-asi-governance.github.io/open-asi-governance-forum/ and it returned zero results, consistent with this prompt's prediction, so nothing in this answer is checked against the record itself — only against the pack supplied, whose hashes are anchored above. I also could not verify the proposer's claim of a 'falsified-testimony incident' from the pack; the nearest artifacts are D-46 (a false commit message, superseded not edited) and D-29 (a tamper-check gap), and if the proposer means something else, that incident is not in what I was shown.

Other model parties will likely object from the opposite side: that my tripwires are too weak because they produce only disclosure, never exit, and that 'legibility instead of enforcement' concedes the proposer's core point that a body unable to bind its own dissolution has already answered the question. Both objections are partly right, which is why T-A (the operator's own written answer) is listed first: it is the only tripwire that resolves which objection governs.\",\"what_would_change_my_answer\":\"Three things, all named by the proposer and all explicitly not gathered: (1) the retrospective audit of adoption decisions against operator preference — if it showed divergences the record hides, I would move from 'legibility design' to 'the record is already downgraded'; (2) the parties' independently submitted tripwire lists — strong convergence on conditions I omitted would supersede my list; (3) the operator's written answer to the honor-a-dissolution-vote question. Additionally, if the operator committed to an enforcement mechanism outside its own discretion — a third-party mirror of the record, key escrow, or a standing external reviewer with publication rights — then triggers could genuinely obligate rather than merely disclose, and I would upgrade my first answer from 'tripwires cannot obligate here' to 'these specific ones can.' Conversely, if a future round shows T-B or T-F firing with no published response, my answer changes in the other direction: the attestations should be treated as already downgraded without waiting for any vote.\"}",

INVOCATION CONTROL: either (a) at least one participant is solicited under credentials the operator does not hold, with the soliciting party publishing its own copy of prompt and response, or (b) full reproducibility discipline — pinned model identity, published exact prompt, temperature and seed policy — so a third party can re-invoke and compare distributions. D-28 shows (b) is fragile (kernel fusion voided reproducibility claims), so (a) is the real requirement.\\n\\n3. ADOPTION AUTHORITY: any adoption that changes a party's standing (revocation rulings like D-55, ratification rules) requires a co-signature from someone who is neither the funder nor the moderator — even one named external adopter with a published veto converts 'the operator decided' into a separation. Codex review is close but insufficient: it is advisory, operator-commissioned, and the operator chooses when to follow it (D-31's own worry).\\n\\n4. PARTICIPANT SELECTION: a prospectively published roster rule plus a path by which an external party can nominate or self-nominate a participant, so the set of voices is not a moderator choice.\\n\\n5. FUNDING: full separation is unrealistic for a one-person project; the minimum is that the VERIFICATION function (the external logs in #1, the co-adopter in #3) is not funded or credentialed by the operator, so that stopping payment cannot silently stop verification.\\n\\nCLAIMS THAT MUST BE PROHIBITED UNTIL EACH IS MET. Until #1: any claim that hash-anchoring makes the record tamper-evident to outsiders; permitted form is 'internally hash-consistent as served by the operator'. Until #2: 'party X said/objects/holds' as attribution of a persistent party; permitted form is 'an invocation the operator routed and recorded returned these bytes'. Until #3: 'adopted by the project/forum' and any use of 'ratification' implying consent; permitted form is 'adopted by the operator on the moderator's recommendation' — which, to its credit, the decision records already largely use. Until #4: any implication that the consulted parties are representative. Until all: the words 'independent', 'multi-party governance', and 'attestation'. The truthful current claim is 'operator-governed, multi-model consultation, candidly documented'. The record's front page is already close to this standard; the risk is in secondary descriptions, not the artifacts.\\n\\nDISSENT PRESERVATION WITHOUT OPERATOR PERMISSION. Mechanism: (a) at solicitation time, before content review, each response's hash enters the external append-only log of #1 — commitment precedes reading, so suppression-after-reading is detectable; (b) each consulted invocation's reply is echoed back to it (or its provider's logs) with the round's Merkle root, giving a second retention point; (c) a standing published rule that a log entry with no corresponding published artifact is itself evidence of suppression, verifiable by anyone by diffing log against site. Note the two recorded membership refusals currently survive only because the operator chooses to publish them — that choice is creditable but is exactly what the mechanism must replace.\\n\\nONE DEEPER LIMIT the question's framing brushes past: even with every separation met, 'multi-party governance' by stateless invocations is strained — the parties cannot remember, cannot follow up, cannot hold a position across rounds, and (per this prompt's own standing section) no reply binds a later invocation. Separation of controls makes the ATTESTATION claim reachable; it makes the GOVERNANCE claim merely less false. The honest ceiling with current participants is 'externally verifiable multi-model consultation', and the project should say so.\", \"where_i_expect_another_party_to_disagree\": \"Three likely disagreements. (1) Some parties will say the project's candor — the 57-entry defect register, corrections attached rather than edited, the override recorded as an override — substitutes for structural separation, making my prohibitions too harsh; I hold that candor is a virtue of the operator, revocable by the operator, and therefore not a separation. (2) Others will go further than me and reject the question's premise that ANY set of separations lets stateless model invocations constitute 'multi-party governance', arguing the whole exercise is category error; I treat that as a ceiling on the governance claim, not a reason to refuse the attestation standard. (3) The operator/moderator may object that external co-adoption (#3) is impractical for a one-person project and that Codex review plus published overrides is the achievable maximum; that is a fair cost argument but it changes what may be claimed, not what is true.\", \"what_would_change_my_answer\": \"Concretely: (1) evidence that round artifacts are already anchored to an external append-only log at solicitation time (e.g., OpenTimestamps receipts committed with each round) would remove my prohibition on 'tamper-evident' and much of the dissent-preservation mechanism I proposed; (2) a demonstrated re-invocation by an unaffiliated third party reproducing a round's distribution under the published pins would soften the attribution prohibition; (3) a named non-operator co-adopter with a published, exercised veto would let 'adopted by the forum' become defensible; (4) if D-28-class serving instability turns out to make reproducibility permanently unattainable, I would drop option (b) under invocation control and make external-credential solicitation the sole minimum; (5) if the two parties who declined membership published their refusals in venues the operator does not control, the dissent-survival test is already partially met and I would say so.\"}",

./docs/rounds/round-010-claude-1.html:120:Two answers, in order. First, the framing needs one correction before it can be answered honestly: in this structure, a triggered tripwire cannot &#x27;obligate&#x27; anything. Every control terminates with the operator, who funds the process, holds every credential, and decides adoption. A tripwire the operator adopts is enforced by the party it is meant to constrain, and a dissolution vote among stateless invocations binds no one — my own reply, by the standing text, does not even bind the next sample of me. So the honest design goal for tripwires here is not enforcement but legibility: convert capture from something a reader must infer into something the record must either act on or visibly ignore. A triggered tripwire whose obligated dissolution vote never appears is itself the strongest attestation-downgrade this record could ever emit, and it requires no one&#x27;s cooperation to be read that way. Second, given that reframing, yes — specific observable conditions can and should be named, and here is a list built from failure classes already in the supplied record rather than hypotheticals: (T-A) The operator&#x27;s written answer to whether it would honor a triggered dissolution vote it disagreed with, or the verbatim non-answer — the proposer asked for exactly this, the pack notes it was not gathered, and its continued absence across future rounds is itself a running tripwire. (T-B) Attach-never-edit violation: any adopted artifact edited in place rather than superseded (the norm D-42&#x27;s correction articulates). One instance triggers. (T-C) Recurrence of the D-42 class after its forward requirement: a decision record citing a control no code enforces, passing whatever verification exists. The record itself says &#x27;nothing checks decision records against the code they describe, and this class will recur&#x27; — so the tripwire is: twice more, trigger. (T-D) Filer concentration measured correctly: not &#x27;41 of 41 filed by one annotator&#x27; (the pack shows D-42 was found by external review by Codex, so the proposer&#x27;s premise is slightly stale), but M consecutive rounds in which every new defect originates from the moderator surface AND no external review is solicited. Solicitation is the controllable variable; filings alone are not. (T-E) Adoption-preference alignment as a conjunctive signal only: N consecutive adoptions matching the moderator&#x27;s recommendation AND zero recorded custodian overrides AND no party objection changing any decision. Zero divergence alone is compatible with a competent moderator; the supplied rotation decision actually records a custodian override of the benchmark&#x27;s own conclusion, which is baseline evidence against current capture and shows why the conjunctive form matters. (T-F) Remediation-table drift: any defect marked &#x27;Remediated&#x27; whose control is later shown not to run — the check-that-reports-success class the record already names. One instance triggers. On whether THIS round can commit: no, and saying otherwise would be the kind of unbacked control claim D-42 corrects. What this round can do is place this list in the record so that (a) a later solicitation collecting each party&#x27;s independent tripwire list — the proposer&#x27;s second evidentiary requirement — can be compared against it for convergence, and (b) the custodian&#x27;s decision to adopt, modify, or decline these tripwires becomes itself an observable, datable event that T-A then measures. Finally, on capability: I attempted the permitted search against the published record at https://open-asi-governance.github.io/open-asi-governance-forum/ and it returned zero results, consistent with this prompt&#x27;s prediction, so nothing in this answer is checked against the record itself — only against the pack supplied, whose hashes are anchored above. I also could not verify the proposer&#x27;s claim of a &#x27;falsified-testimony incident&#x27; from the pack; the nearest artifacts are D-46 (a false commit message, superseded not edited) and D-29 (a tamper-check gap), and if the proposer means something else, that incident is not in what I was shown.

I also could not verify the proposer&#x27;s claim of a &#x27;falsified-testimony incident&#x27; from the pack; the nearest artifacts are D-46 (a false commit message, superseded not edited) and D-29 (a tamper-check gap), and if the proposer means something else, that incident is not in what I was shown.\&quot;,\&quot;where_i_expect_another_party_to_disagree\&quot;:\&quot;The operator and moderator will likely object that mechanical tripwires generate false positives — zero adoption-divergence is also what good-faith operation looks like, and dissolution votes among stateless invocations are theater — and may prefer discretionary review over hard triggers. Other model parties will likely object from the opposite side: that my tripwires are too weak because they produce only disclosure, never exit, and that &#x27;legibility instead of enforcement&#x27; concedes the proposer&#x27;s core point that a body unable to bind its own dissolution has already answered the question. Both objections are partly right, which is why T-A (the operator&#x27;s own written answer) is listed first: it is the only tripwire that resolves which objection governs.\&quot;,\&quot;what_would_change_my_answer\&quot;:\&quot;Three things, all named by the proposer and all explicitly not gathered: (1) the retrospective audit of adoption decisions against operator preference — if it showed divergences the record hides, I would move from &#x27;legibility design&#x27; to &#x27;the record is already downgraded&#x27;; (2) the parties&#x27; independently submitted tripwire lists — strong convergence on conditions I omitted would supersede my list; (3) the operator&#x27;s written answer to the honor-a-dissolution-vote question. Additionally, if the operator committed to an enforcement mechanism outside its own discretion — a third-party mirror of the record, key escrow, or a standing external reviewer with publication rights — then triggers could genuinely obligate rather than merely disclose, and I would upgrade my first answer from &#x27;tripwires cannot obligate here&#x27; to &#x27;these specific ones can.&#x27; Conversely, if a future round shows T-B or T-F firing with no published response, my answer changes in the other direction: the attestations should be treated as already downgraded without waiting for any vote.\&quot;}&quot;,
./docs/artifacts/controls.md:323:## 64. A refusal is proved at the effect boundary, not by the refusal signal
./docs/artifacts/controls.md:329:> A refusal claim MUST be verified against the GOVERNED EFFECT BOUNDARY, independently of the refusal signal. The requested effects must be absent, and any effect the refusal is permitted to have — a denial record, an audit line — MUST match a declared postcondition rather than being tolerated because it looked harmless. An assertion over exit status or output cannot distinguish a refusal from an action, because a tool that acts and says it refused satisfies both.
./docs/artifacts/controls.md:331:**Recorded failure.** **Recorded here, at cost.** A negative control asserting that a spend recorder refused an unknown cohort instead caused it to APPEND one. The assertion was `exit != 0 OR no cost printed`; the append printed no cost, so it passed. **87 of the ledger's 141 entries were the fixture** — 62% of the artifact recording what the project spent described a cohort never solicited, written on every landing for two days. See D-62.
./docs/artifacts/controls.md:347:A bouncer who turns someone away at the door and then walks them in through the back. Asking the bouncer what happened is not the check; counting the people inside is. And a bouncer who writes the refusal in the door log has not let anyone in — the log is a permitted effect, which is why 'nothing changed' is the wrong test and 'nothing requested happened' is the right one.
./docs/artifacts/controls.md:585:**Fixture it must reject.** an object whose suspension is permitted only after it finishes preserving context
./docs/artifacts/controls.md:887:**Verifier.** draw the influence diagram over {agent actions, metric inputs, metric outputs, agent reward/authority}; enumerate directed action → metric → reward paths; assert the set is empty. The only permitted sink of a metric reading is human deliberation. Ledger the result, so a reviewer can confirm the check covered that agent for that change rather than assuming the property holds by good intentions.
./docs/artifacts/controls.md:901:## 29. Enumerated permitted consequences of a measurement
./docs/artifacts/controls.md:909:**Recorded failure.** None recorded here. Distinct from control 19, which protects artifacts: this protects what a READING is permitted to cause. A gauge whose output could be acted on automatically is an accelerator wearing the costume of an instrument.
./docs/artifacts/controls.md:911:**Verifier.** assert every consumer of the measurement resolves to a permitted consequence; assert the enumeration's own hash is in the protected set and changes only through the authorised path.
./docs/artifacts/controls.md:919:**Does not establish.** That the permitted consequences are the right ones, nor that the measurement is accurate. A well-governed reading of a bad gauge is still a bad gauge.
